8014cb12ab.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between śaniḥ and śukraḥ in rēvatī mīnaḥ, center-to-center separation 0°36′15.67″.
8014cb12ab.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°36′15.67″, 0°36′02.25″ apart, disc-to-disc. śaniḥ at rēvatī-4 mīnaḥ (latitude 2°15′32.13″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude +0.71, elongation 25°42′15.53″ W). śukraḥ at rēvatī-4 mīnaḥ (latitude 1°39′16.46″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -3.87, elongation 25°39′41.05″ W). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here śaniḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śaniḥ is taken as jayI over śukraḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

𑌵𑍈𑌶𑌾𑌖 𑌶𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇 𑌤𑍃𑌤𑍀𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌹𑌲𑌾𑌯𑍁𑌧𑌃।  
𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌷𑌣𑍋 𑌬𑌲𑍋 𑌜𑌜𑍍𑌞𑍇 𑌰𑌾𑌮𑌃 𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌾𑌗𑍍𑌰𑌜𑍋 𑌹𑌰𑌿𑌃॥  
𑌅𑌵𑌤𑌾𑌰𑌦𑌿𑌨𑍇 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑍇 𑌹𑌰𑌿𑌮𑍁𑌦𑍍𑌦𑌿𑌶𑍍𑌯 𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌤𑌃।  
𑌉𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌾𑌦𑌿 𑌯𑌤𑍍 𑌕𑌿𑌞𑍍𑌚𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌦𑌾𑌨𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯 𑌕𑌲𑍍𑌪𑌤𑍇॥  
—𑌸𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑌿𑌮𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌫𑌲𑌮𑍍  
𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌨𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌯𑌕𑌲𑍍𑌪𑌵𑌲𑍍𑌲𑍀---  
𑌇𑌯𑌮𑍇𑌵 𑌬𑌲𑌰𑌾𑌮𑌜𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍀। 𑌸𑌾 𑌮𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌨𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌪𑌿𑌨𑍀 𑌗𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌯𑌾। 𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌚𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌂 𑌸𑍍𑌕𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍇---  
𑌵𑍈𑌶𑌾𑌖𑍇 𑌶𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇 𑌤𑍁 𑌤𑍃𑌤𑍀𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌗𑍁𑌰𑍌 𑌤𑌥𑌾।  
𑌰𑍋𑌹𑌿𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌕𑌟𑍇 𑌲𑌗𑍍𑌨𑍇 𑌬𑌲𑌰𑌾𑌮𑍋 𑌭𑌵𑍇𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌰𑌿𑌃॥ 𑌇𑌤𑌿।  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌨𑌾𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌃—  
𑌨𑌮𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌹𑌲𑌿𑌨𑌾𑌂 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌷𑍍𑌠 𑌨𑌮𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌮𑍁𑌸𑌲𑌾𑌯𑍁𑌧।  
𑌨𑌮𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌰𑍇𑌵𑌤𑍀𑌕𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤 𑌨𑌮𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌵𑌤𑍍𑌸𑌲॥  
𑌨𑌮𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌬𑌲𑌿𑌨𑌾𑌂 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌷𑍍𑌠 𑌨𑌮𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌧𑌰𑌣𑍀𑌧𑌰।  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌲𑌮𑍍𑌬𑌘𑍍𑌨 𑌨𑌮𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍇𑌽𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑌿 𑌮𑌾𑌂 𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌜॥

---𑌸𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑌿𑌕𑍌𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁𑌭𑍇  
𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌕𑌰𑌣𑍇 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌵𑌾𑌯𑌮𑌾𑌹 𑌶𑌾𑌤𑌾𑌤𑌪𑌃—  
𑌸𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌮𑌣𑍇 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑍇 𑌨 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌦𑌿 𑌮𑌾𑌨𑌵𑌃।  
𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌜𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌸𑍁 𑌰𑍋𑌗𑍀 𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑍍 𑌦𑍁𑌃𑌖𑌭𑌾𑌗𑍀 𑌚 𑌜𑌾𑌯𑌤𑍇॥  
𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌯𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌹𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌕𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌮𑌾𑌨𑌵𑍈𑌃।  
𑌤𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌦𑌦𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌰𑍍𑌕𑌃 𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌜𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌸𑍁 𑌨𑌿𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌿𑌤𑌮𑍍॥  
---𑌵𑍈𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌨𑌾𑌥-𑌦𑍀𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌿𑌤𑍀𑌯𑍇 𑌸𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑌿𑌮𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌫𑌲𑍇 𑌆𑌹𑍍𑌨𑌿𑌕-𑌕𑌾𑌣𑍍𑌡𑌃 (𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌭𑌾𑌗𑌃)  
𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌮𑌾𑌨𑍇 𑌤𑍁𑌲𑌾𑌮𑍇𑌷𑍇 𑌨𑌾𑌡𑍍𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍂𑌭𑌯𑌤𑍋 𑌦𑌶।  
𑌯𑌾 𑌯𑌾𑌃 𑌸𑌨𑍍𑌨𑌿𑌹𑌿𑌤𑌾 𑌨𑌾𑌡𑍍𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌤𑌮𑌾𑌃 𑌸𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑌾𑌃॥  
---𑌵𑍈𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌨𑌾𑌥-𑌦𑍀𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌿𑌤𑍀𑌯𑍇 𑌸𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑌿𑌮𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌫𑌲𑍇 𑌆𑌹𑍍𑌨𑌿𑌕-𑌕𑌾𑌣𑍍𑌡𑌃 (𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌭𑌾𑌗𑌃)

8128ce4237.b: Observed on Śukla-Trayōdaśī tithi of Vaiśākhaḥ (lunar) month (Sūryōdayaḥ/puurvaviddha).
8128ce4237.d: Last three days of vaiśākha-māsaḥ. anantaphaladam! Perform Shiva/Vishnu Puja, Bhagavata Parayanam, BhagavadGita Parayanam, Vishnu Sahasranama Parayanam, dāna of apūpa, pāyasa etc.
8128ce4237.s:
𑌯𑌃 𑌮𑌾𑌧𑌵𑍇 𑌵𑍈𑌶𑌾𑌖𑌮𑌾𑌸𑍇, 𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍋𑌦𑌶𑍀𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌦𑌶𑍀𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌿𑌮𑌾𑌸𑍁 𑌤𑌿𑌥𑌿𑌷𑍁 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌕𑌂 𑌕𑌰𑍋𑌤𑌿  
𑌸 𑌨𑌿𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌯𑍇𑌨 𑌮𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌨𑍁𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍। 𑌯𑌥𑌾 𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾 𑌧𑌨𑌶𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌾 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌣𑌃 𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌤𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌚  
𑌮𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌿𑌤𑌿। 𑌅𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌸𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌾 𑌕𑌥𑌾 𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌦𑌶𑌾𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌮𑌕𑌪𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌮𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌵𑍈𑌶𑌾𑌖𑌮𑌾𑌹𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌮𑍍𑌯𑍇।  
𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾 𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌨𑌾 𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍋𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌹𑌿𑌰𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌃, 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌮𑌧𑍁𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌘𑌾𑌤𑌿𑌤𑌃,  
𑌪𑍌𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌮𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌭𑍂𑌮𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌾𑌰𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌕𑍃𑌤𑌃, 𑌤𑌤𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌭𑍃𑌤𑌿 𑌤𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌥𑌯𑌃 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌜𑌾𑌤𑌾𑌃!  
𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍁𑌤𑌦𑍇𑌵 𑌉𑌵𑌾𑌚---  
𑌯𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌥𑌯𑌃 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌅𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌮𑌾𑌃 𑌶𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌕𑍇।  
𑌵𑍈𑌶𑌾𑌖𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌿 𑌰𑌾𑌜𑍇𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌿𑌮𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌃 𑌶𑍁𑌭𑌾𑌵𑌹𑌾𑌃॥௧॥  
𑌅𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌕𑌰𑌿𑌣𑍀𑌸𑌂𑌜𑍍𑌞𑌾𑌃 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌯𑌾𑌵𑌹𑌾𑌃।  
𑌮𑌾𑌧𑌵𑍇 𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌿 𑌯𑌃 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌂 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌤𑍁𑌂 𑌨 𑌚 𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌮𑌃॥௨॥  
𑌤𑌿𑌥𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌵𑍇𑌤𑌾𑌸𑍁 𑌸 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌮𑍇𑌵 𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌲𑌭𑍇𑌤𑍍।  
𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍇 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍋𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑍍𑌥𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌜𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍂𑌨𑍍𑌪𑍁𑌨𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌹𑌿॥௩॥  
𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌤𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌥𑍈𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌨𑌾 𑌸𑌹 𑌸𑌂𑌸𑍍𑌥𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌃।  
𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑌯𑌜𑍍𑌞𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌾 𑌏𑌤𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌪𑍁𑌨𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌹𑌿॥௪॥  
𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌘𑍍𑌨𑌂 𑌵𑌾 𑌸𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌪𑌂 𑌵𑌾 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌨𑍇𑌤𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌪𑍁𑌨𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌹𑌿।  
𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾 𑌜𑌜𑍍𑌞𑍇 𑌵𑍈𑌶𑌾𑌖𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑌮𑍃𑌤𑌂 𑌶𑍁𑌭𑌮𑍍॥௫॥  
𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌪𑌾𑌲𑌿𑌤𑌂 𑌤𑌚𑍍𑌚 𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌨𑌾 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌭𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌨𑌾।  
𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍋𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑍁𑌧𑌾𑌂 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌪𑌾𑌯𑌯𑌾𑌮𑌾𑌸 𑌵𑍈 𑌹𑌰𑌿𑌃॥௬॥  
𑌜𑌘𑌾𑌨 𑌚 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌦𑍈𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌵𑌿𑌰𑍋𑌧𑌿𑌨𑌃।  
𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑌾𑌮𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌜𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌬𑌭𑍂𑌵 𑌹॥௭॥  
𑌤𑌤𑍋 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌾𑌃 𑌸𑍁𑌸𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌾 𑌏𑌤𑌾𑌸𑌾𑌂 𑌚 𑌵𑌰𑌂 𑌦𑌦𑍁𑌃।  
𑌤𑌿𑌸𑍃𑌣𑌾𑌂 𑌚 𑌤𑌿𑌥𑍀𑌨𑌾𑌂 𑌵𑍈 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌤𑍍𑌯𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌫𑍁𑌲𑍍𑌲𑌵𑌿𑌲𑍋𑌚𑌨𑌾𑌃॥௮॥  
𑌏𑌤𑌾 𑌵𑍈𑌶𑌾𑌖𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌤𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌤𑌿𑌥𑌯𑌃 𑌶𑍁𑌭𑌾𑌃।  
𑌪𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌪𑍌𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌫𑌲𑌦𑌾 𑌨𑌰𑌾𑌣𑌾𑌂 𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌹𑌾𑌨𑌿𑌦𑌾𑌃॥௯॥  
𑌯𑍋𑌽𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌸𑍇 𑌚 𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑍇 𑌨 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍋 𑌮𑌨𑍁𑌜𑌾𑌧𑌮𑌃।  
𑌤𑌿𑌥𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍇 𑌤𑍁 𑌸 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌮𑍇𑌵 𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌲𑌭𑍇𑌤𑍍॥௧௦॥  
𑌤𑌿𑌥𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍇𑌽𑌪𑍍𑌯𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌣𑌃 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌦𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌕𑌂 𑌨𑌰𑌃।  
𑌚𑌾𑌣𑍍𑌡𑌾𑌲𑍀𑌂 𑌯𑍋𑌨𑌿𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯 𑌪𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌰𑍌𑌰𑌵𑌮𑌶𑍍𑌨𑍁𑌤𑍇॥௧௧॥  
𑌉𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍋𑌦𑌕𑍇𑌨 𑌯𑌃 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌤𑌿 𑌮𑌾𑌧𑌵𑍇 𑌚 𑌤𑌿𑌥𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍇।  
𑌰𑍌𑌰𑌵𑌂 𑌨𑌰𑌕𑌂 𑌯𑌾𑌤𑌿 𑌯𑌾𑌵𑌦𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌦𑌶॥௧௨॥  
𑌪𑌿𑌤𑍄𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌸𑌮𑍁𑌦𑍍𑌦𑌿𑌶𑍍𑌯 𑌦𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌨𑌂 𑌨 𑌦𑌦𑌾𑌤𑌿 𑌯𑌃।  
𑌪𑍈𑌶𑌾𑌚𑍀𑌂 𑌯𑍋𑌨𑌿𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯 𑌤𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌠𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌭𑍂𑌤𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌪𑍍𑌲𑌵𑌮𑍍॥௧௩॥  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌵𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌂 𑌚 𑌕𑌾𑌮𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌂 𑌮𑌾𑌧𑌵𑍇 𑌨𑌿𑌯𑌮𑍇 𑌕𑍃𑌤𑍇।  
𑌅𑌵𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌸𑌾𑌯𑍁𑌜𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌯𑍁𑌜𑍍𑌯𑌤𑍇 𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌸𑌂𑌶𑌯𑌃॥௧௪॥  
𑌆𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌂 𑌨𑌿𑌯𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌃 𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌦𑌿 𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍇।  
𑌤𑍇𑌨 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌯 𑌮𑍋𑌦𑌤𑍇 𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌦𑌿𑌰𑍇॥௧௫॥  
𑌯𑍋 𑌵𑍈 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌪𑌿𑌤𑍄𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌂 𑌗𑍁𑌰𑍁𑌮𑍁𑌦𑍍𑌦𑌿𑌶𑍍𑌯 𑌮𑌾𑌨𑌵𑌃।  
𑌨 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌦𑌿 𑌕𑌰𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌾𑌽𑌮𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌯 𑌶𑌾𑌪𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌦𑌾 𑌵𑌯𑌮𑍍॥௧௬॥  
𑌨𑌿𑌃𑌸𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌨𑍋 𑌨𑌿𑌰𑌾𑌯𑍁𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌨𑌿𑌃𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌕𑍋 𑌭𑌵𑍇𑌦𑌿𑌤𑌿।  
𑌇𑌤𑌿 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌾 𑌵𑌰𑌂 𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌧𑌾𑌮𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌯𑌯𑍁𑌃 𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾॥௧௭॥  
𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌥𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑌂 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌘𑍌𑌘𑌵𑌿𑌨𑌾𑌶𑌨𑌮𑍍।  
𑌅𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌪𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌕𑌰𑌿𑌣𑍀𑌸𑌂𑌜𑍍𑌞𑌂 𑌪𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌪𑍌𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌵𑌿𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌧𑌨𑌮𑍍॥௧௮॥  
𑌯𑌾 𑌨𑌾𑌰𑍀 𑌸𑍁𑌭𑌗𑌾𑌽𑌪𑍂𑌪𑌪𑌾𑌯𑌸𑌂 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌿𑌮𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌨𑍇।  
𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌣𑌾𑌯 𑌸𑌕𑍃𑌦𑍍𑌦𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌕𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌂 𑌸𑍁𑌤𑌂 𑌲𑌭𑍇𑌤𑍍॥௧௯॥  
𑌗𑍀𑌤𑌾𑌪𑌾𑌠𑌂 𑌤𑍁 𑌯𑌃 𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌮𑍇 𑌚 𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍇।  
𑌦𑌿𑌨𑍇𑌦𑌿𑌨𑍇𑌽𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌮𑍇𑌧𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌂 𑌫𑌲𑌮𑍇𑌤𑌿 𑌨 𑌸𑌂𑌶𑌯𑌃॥௨௦॥  
𑌸𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌨𑌾𑌮𑌪𑌠𑌨𑌂 𑌯𑌃 𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌯𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌚𑍍𑌚 𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍇।  
𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌵𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍁𑌂 𑌕𑌃 𑌶𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍋 𑌦𑌿𑌵𑌿 𑌵𑌾 𑌭𑍁𑌵𑌿॥௨௧॥  
𑌸𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌨𑌾𑌮𑌭𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌂 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌮𑌧𑍁𑌸𑍂𑌦𑌨𑌮𑍍।  
𑌪𑌯𑌸𑌾 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌯 𑌵𑍈 𑌯𑌾𑌤𑌿 𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌲𑍋𑌕𑌮𑌕𑌲𑍍𑌮𑌷𑌮𑍍॥௨௨॥  
𑌸𑌮𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌵𑌿𑌭𑌵𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌪𑍂𑌜𑌯𑍇𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌧𑍁𑌸𑍂𑌦𑌨𑌮𑍍।  
𑌨 𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌲𑍋𑌕𑌾𑌃 𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍀𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌯𑍁𑌗 𑌕𑌲𑍍𑌪𑌾𑌦𑌿 𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌯𑍇॥௨௩॥  
𑌅𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌚𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌯𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌚 𑌵𑍈𑌶𑌾𑌖𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌮𑌤𑍋 𑌯𑌦𑌿।  
𑌸 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌹𑌾 𑌗𑍁𑌰𑍁𑌘𑍍𑌨𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌪𑌿𑌤𑍄𑌣𑌾𑌂 𑌘𑌾𑌤𑌕𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌥𑌾॥௨௪॥  
𑌶𑍍𑌲𑍋𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌧𑌂 𑌶𑍍𑌲𑍋𑌕𑌪𑌾𑌦𑌂 𑌵𑌾 𑌨𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌭𑌾𑌗𑌵𑌤𑍋𑌦𑍍𑌭𑌵𑌮𑍍।  
𑌵𑍈𑌶𑌾𑌖𑍇 𑌚 𑌪𑌠𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌰𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑍋 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌂 𑌚𑍋𑌪𑌪𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌤𑍇॥௨௫॥  
𑌯𑍋 𑌵𑍈 𑌭𑌾𑌗𑌵𑌤𑌂 𑌶𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌂 𑌶𑍃𑌣𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌯𑍇𑌤𑌦𑍍𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍇।  
𑌨 𑌪𑌾𑌪𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌲𑌿𑌪𑍍𑌯𑌤𑍇 𑌕𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌪𑌿 𑌪𑌦𑍍𑌮𑌪𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌮𑌿𑌵𑌾𑌮𑍍𑌭𑌸𑌾॥௨௬॥  
𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌂 𑌮𑌨𑍁𑌜𑍈𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌂 𑌕𑍈𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌸𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌮𑍇𑌵 𑌚।  
𑌕𑍈𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌤𑍋 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌭𑌾𑌵𑍋 𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑌨𑌿𑌷𑍇𑌵𑌣𑌾𑌤𑍍॥௨௭॥  
𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌜𑍍𑌞𑌾𑌨𑍇𑌨 𑌵𑍈 𑌮𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌯𑌾𑌗𑌮𑌰𑌣𑍇𑌨 𑌵𑌾।  
𑌅𑌥𑌵𑌾 𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌿 𑌵𑍈𑌶𑌾𑌖𑍇 𑌨𑌿𑌯𑌮𑍇𑌨 𑌜𑌲𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌲𑍁𑌤𑍇𑌃॥௨௮॥  
𑌨𑍀𑌲𑌵𑍃𑌷𑌂 𑌸𑌮𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌸𑍃𑌜𑍍𑌯 𑌵𑍈𑌶𑌾𑌖𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌚 𑌜𑌲𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌲𑍁𑌤𑍇𑌃।  
𑌸𑌮𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌬𑌨𑍍𑌧𑌨𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌮𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌃 𑌪𑍁𑌮𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌤𑌿 𑌪𑌰𑌂 𑌪𑌦𑌮𑍍॥௨௯॥  
𑌗𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑌵𑌤𑍍𑌸𑌾𑌂 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌜𑍇𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌯 𑌸𑍀𑌦𑌤𑍇 𑌚 𑌕𑍁𑌟𑍁𑌮𑍍𑌬𑌿𑌨𑍇।  
𑌇𑌹𑌾𑌪𑌮𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌨𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌮𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌃 𑌪𑌰𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌚 𑌪𑌰𑌂 𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌜𑍇𑌤𑍍॥௩௦॥  
𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌦𑌾𑌨𑌵𑌿𑌹𑍀𑌨𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌵𑍈𑌶𑌾𑌖𑍀 𑌚𑍈𑌵 𑌯𑍋 𑌨𑌯𑍇𑌤𑍍।  
𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌨𑌯𑍋𑌨𑌿𑌶𑌤𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌯 𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌠𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌜𑌾𑌯𑌤𑍇 𑌕𑍃𑌮𑌿𑌃॥௩௧॥  
𑌤𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌃 𑌕𑍋𑌟𑍍𑌯𑍋𑌽𑌰𑍍𑌧𑌕𑍋𑌟𑌿𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌤𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌭𑍁𑌵𑌨𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍇।  
𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌭𑍂𑌯 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑌾𑌞𑍍𑌚𑌕𑍍𑌰𑍁𑌃 𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌘𑌾𑌤𑌶𑌙𑍍𑌕𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌃॥௩௨॥  
𑌜𑌨𑌾 𑌅𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌸𑍁 𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌠𑌾 𑌵𑌿𑌸𑍃𑌜𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌕𑌂 𑌮𑌲𑌮𑍍।  
𑌤𑌦𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌕𑌂 𑌕𑌥𑌂 𑌗𑌚𑍍𑌛𑍇𑌦𑌿𑌤𑌿 𑌚𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌸𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌃॥௩௩॥  
𑌤𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌪𑌾𑌦𑌂 𑌹𑌰𑌿𑌂 𑌜𑌗𑍍𑌮𑍁𑌃 𑌶𑌰𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌶𑌰𑌣𑌂 𑌵𑌿𑌭𑍁𑌮𑍍।  
𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌚 𑌬𑌹𑍁𑌭𑌿𑌃 𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍈𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌯𑌾𑌮𑌾𑌸𑍁𑌰𑌞𑍍𑌜𑌸𑌾॥௩௪॥  
𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌦𑍇𑌵 𑌜𑌗𑌨𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌥 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌘𑍌𑌘𑌵𑌿𑌨𑌾𑌶𑌨।  
𑌜𑌨𑌾 𑌅𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌸𑍁 𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌠𑌾𑌃 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌶𑌃॥௩௫॥  
𑌵𑌿𑌸𑍃𑌜𑍍𑌯 𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌤𑍍𑌪𑌦𑌂 𑌯𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌦𑌾𑌜𑍍𑌞𑌾𑌧𑌾𑌰𑌿𑌣𑍋 𑌭𑍁𑌵𑌿।  
𑌅𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌕𑌂 𑌚𑍈𑌵 𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌂 𑌕𑌥𑌂 𑌗𑌚𑍍𑌛𑍇𑌜𑍍𑌜𑌨𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌦𑌨॥௩௬॥  
𑌤𑌦𑍁𑌪𑌾𑌯𑌂 𑌵𑌦𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌕𑌂 𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌤𑍍𑌪𑌾𑌦𑌶𑌰𑌣𑍈𑌷𑌿𑌣𑌾𑌮𑍍।  
𑌇𑌤𑌿 𑌤𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌥𑍈𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌿𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌭𑌗𑌵𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌭𑍂𑌤𑌭𑌾𑌵𑌨𑌃॥௩௭॥  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌹𑌸𑌨𑍍𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹 𑌤𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌮𑍇𑌘𑌗𑌮𑍍𑌭𑍀𑌰𑌯𑌾 𑌗𑌿𑌰𑌾।  
𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌭𑌗𑌵𑌾𑌨𑍁𑌵𑌾𑌚---  
𑌸𑌿𑌤𑍇 𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇 𑌮𑍇𑌷𑌸𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌯𑍇 𑌵𑍈𑌶𑌾𑌖𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍇𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍇॥௩௮॥  
𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌤𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌮𑌯𑍇 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑍇 𑌮𑌮𑌾𑌪𑌿 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌣𑌵𑌲𑍍𑌲𑌭𑍇।  
𑌯𑍂𑌯𑌂 𑌭𑌗𑍋𑌦𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌂 𑌬𑌹𑌿𑌃𑌸𑌂𑌸𑍍𑌥𑌜𑌲𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌲𑍁𑌤𑌾𑌃॥௩௯॥  
𑌵𑌿𑌮𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌘𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌰𑍂𑌪𑌾 𑌭𑌵𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌶𑍁 𑌸𑍁𑌨𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌲𑌾𑌃।  
𑌭𑌵𑌦𑍍𑌭𑌿𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌵𑌿𑌮𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌘𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌯𑍇 𑌨 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌤𑌾 𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍇॥௪௦॥  
𑌤𑍇𑌷𑍁 𑌤𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌠𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌂 𑌜𑌨𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌮𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌰𑍇𑌚𑌿𑌤𑌮𑍍।  
𑌇𑌤𑌿 𑌤𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌪𑌦𑍋 𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌂 𑌚 𑌵𑌰𑌂 𑌦𑌦𑍌॥௪௧॥  
𑌅𑌨𑍁𑌜𑍍𑌞𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌯 𑌚 𑌤𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌯𑍋𑌗𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍈𑌵𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌰𑌧𑍀𑌯𑌤।  
𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌧𑌾𑌮𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌪𑍁𑌨𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌯 𑌤𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌤𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌨𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌶𑌃॥௪௨॥  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌿𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌷𑌂 𑌤𑍁 𑌵𑍈𑌶𑌾𑌖𑍇 𑌤𑌥𑍈𑌵𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍇।  
𑌤𑍇𑌨𑌾𑌘𑍌𑌘𑌂 𑌵𑌿𑌮𑍁𑌚𑍍𑌯𑍈𑌵 𑌯𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌨𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌲𑌤𑌾𑌮𑌹𑍋॥௪௩॥  
𑌯𑍇 𑌤𑍁 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌨 𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌵𑍈𑌶𑌾𑌖𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍇।  
𑌤𑍇 𑌭𑌵𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌸𑌮𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌂 𑌜𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌂 𑌪𑌾𑌤𑌕𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌯𑌾𑌃॥௪௪॥  
𑌇𑌤𑌿 𑌶𑌾𑌪𑌂 𑌚 𑌤𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌹𑍍𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌤𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌂 𑌵𑌦𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌚।  
𑌨 𑌤𑍇𑌨 𑌸𑌦𑍃𑌶𑌃 𑌪𑌾𑌪𑍋 𑌯𑍋 𑌨 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍋 𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍇॥௪௫॥  
𑌵𑌿𑌚𑌾𑌰𑌿𑌤𑍇𑌷𑍁 𑌶𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌷𑍁 𑌨 𑌦𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌟𑍋 𑌨 𑌚 𑌵𑍈 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍁𑌤𑌃।  
𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍇 𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌦𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌚𑌨𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌕𑌮𑍍॥௪௬॥  
𑌅𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌥𑌾 𑌨𑌰𑌕𑌂 𑌯𑌾𑌤𑌿 𑌯𑌾𑌵𑌦𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌦𑌶।  
𑌇𑌤𑍍𑌯𑍇𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌮𑌾𑌖𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌤𑌂 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍁𑌤𑌕𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌮𑌤𑍇॥௪௭॥  
---𑌸𑍍𑌕𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌦-𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇 𑌵𑍈𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌵𑌖𑌣𑍍𑌡𑍇 𑌵𑍈𑌶𑌾𑌖𑌮𑌾𑌹𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌮𑍍𑌯𑍇 𑌪𑌞𑍍𑌚𑌵𑌿𑌂𑌶𑍋𑌽𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌃

8131116431.d:
The Shukla-paksha Ekadashi of jyaiṣṭha month is known as pāṇḍava-nirjalā-ēkādaśī.

The fruits of fasting on Ekādaśī are greatly extolled in the Padma Purana—

A person who bathes at Śaṃkhoddhāra and beholds the image of Viṣṇu does not acquire even a sixteenth of the merit earned by fasting on Ekādaśī. O noble king, even if one gives four lakhs of coins on the days of the Sun's transition between Zodiac signs, it does not equal even a sixteenth of the merit from an Ekādaśī fast! Indeed, fasting on Ekādaśī grants the same religious merit as bathing at Prabhāsa during a lunar or solar eclipse. One who drinks the sacred water at Kedāra is freed from rebirth, and likewise, fasting on Ekādaśī removes the cycle of rebirth.

The merit from an Ekādaśī fast is a hundred times greater than the reward of performing an Ashvamedha sacrifice on earth. Fasting on Ekādaśī yields a hundredfold more merit than gifting a thousand cows to a learned brāhmaṇa. Those who fast on Ekādaśī are considered equal to those whose bodies are inhabited by Brahma, Viṣṇu, and Śiva. The merit from observing the Ekādaśī vow is immeasurable, and difficult to obtain even by the Devas. There is no other vow like that of the Ekādaśī, that destroys sins.
8131116431.s:
𑌵𑍃𑌷𑌸𑍍𑌥𑍇 𑌮𑌿𑌥𑍁𑌨𑌸𑍍𑌥𑍇𑌽𑌰𑍍𑌕𑍇 𑌶𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑌾 𑌹𑍍𑌯𑍇𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍀 𑌭𑌵𑍇𑌤𑍍।  
𑌜𑍍𑌯𑍇𑌷𑍍𑌠𑍇 𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌿 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌨𑍇𑌨 𑌸𑍋𑌪𑍋𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌜𑌲𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌜𑌿𑌤𑌾॥  
𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑍇 𑌚𑌾𑌚𑌮𑌨𑍇 𑌚𑍈𑌵 𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌜𑌯𑍇𑌨𑍍𑌨𑍋𑌦𑌕𑌂 𑌬𑍁𑌧𑌃॥  
𑌸𑌂𑌵𑌤𑍍𑌸𑌰𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌮𑌧𑍍𑌯𑍇 𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍋 𑌭𑌵𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌤।  
𑌤𑌾𑌸𑌾𑌂 𑌫𑌲𑌮𑌵𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌨𑍋𑌤𑌿 𑌅𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌮𑍇 𑌨𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌸𑌂𑌶𑌯𑌃॥ (𑌹𑍇𑌮𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌰𑍌-𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌭𑌾𑌰𑌤𑍇 𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌸𑌵𑌚𑌨𑌮𑍍)  
𑌜𑍍𑌯𑍇𑌷𑍍𑌠𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌶𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑍈𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌨𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌜𑌲𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑌮𑍁𑌪𑍋𑌷𑍍𑌯 𑌤𑍁॥௧௪॥  
𑌉𑌦𑌯𑌾𑌦𑍁𑌦𑌯𑌂 𑌯𑌾𑌵𑌦𑍍𑌭𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌕𑌰𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌜𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌮।  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌭𑌾𑌤𑍇 𑌕𑍃𑌤𑌨𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑍁𑌪𑌚𑌾𑌰𑌕𑍈𑌃॥௧௫॥  
𑌹𑍃𑌷𑍀𑌕𑍇𑌶𑌂 𑌸𑌮𑌭𑍍𑌯𑌰𑍍𑌚𑍍𑌯 𑌵𑌿𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌨𑍍 𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌭𑍋𑌜𑍍𑌯 𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌤𑌃।  
𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌂𑌶𑍈𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍀𑌨𑌾𑌂 𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌸𑌮𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌨𑍁𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍॥௧௨௦-௧௬॥  
---𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌬𑍃𑌹𑌨𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌰𑌦𑍀𑌯𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌭𑌾𑌗𑍇 𑌬𑍃𑌹𑌦𑍁𑌪𑌾𑌖𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌨𑍇 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌪𑌾𑌦𑍇 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌶𑌮𑌾𑌸-𑌸𑍍𑌥𑌿𑌤𑍈𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍀𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌕𑌥𑌨𑌂 𑌨𑌾𑌮 𑌵𑌿𑌂𑌶𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌧𑌿𑌕𑌶𑌤𑌤𑌮𑍋𑌽𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌃  
  
𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇 𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇 𑌚 𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌮𑍇𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑍁𑌪𑍋𑌷𑌣𑌮𑍍।  
𑌯𑌦𑍀𑌚𑍍𑌛𑍇𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌸𑌾𑌯𑍁𑌜𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌯𑌂 𑌸𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌤𑌿𑌮𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌮𑌨𑌃।  
𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌨 𑌭𑍁𑌞𑍍𑌜𑍀𑌤 𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌯𑍋𑌰𑍁𑌭𑌯𑍋𑌰𑌪𑌿॥  
  
𑌅𑌦𑍍𑌯 𑌸𑍍𑌥𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌨𑌿𑌰𑌾𑌹𑌾𑌰𑌃 𑌶𑍍𑌵𑍋𑌭𑍂𑌤𑍇 𑌪𑌰𑌮𑍇𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌰।  
𑌭𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑌿 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌡𑌰𑍀𑌕𑌾𑌕𑍍𑌷 𑌶𑌰𑌣𑌂 𑌮𑍇 𑌭𑌵𑌾𑌚𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌤॥  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌮𑌾𑌦𑌾𑌦𑌥𑌵𑌾𑌽𑌽𑌲𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌰𑍇 𑌕𑍇𑌶𑌵 𑌮𑌾𑌧𑌵।  
𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌚 𑌵𑍈 𑌵𑌿𑌘𑍍𑌨𑍋 𑌨 𑌭𑌵𑍇𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌤𑍍𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌸𑌾𑌦𑌤𑌃॥  
--𑌪𑌦𑍍𑌮𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇  
  
𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌵𑍈𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌖𑌣𑍍𑌡𑍇 𑌸𑍌𑌤𑌿𑌶𑍌𑌨𑌕𑌸𑌂𑌵𑌾𑌦𑍇 𑌨𑌾𑌰𑌦𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌿 𑌶𑌿𑌵𑍋𑌪𑌦𑍇𑌶𑍇 𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌵𑌿𑌵𑌰𑌣𑌂 𑌨𑌾𑌮 𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌵𑌿𑌂𑌶𑌤𑌿𑌤𑌮𑍋𑌽𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌃---  
𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑌨𑌾𑌹𑌾𑌰𑌂 𑌗𑍃𑌹𑍀 𑌵𑌿𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌭𑌾𑌰𑌤𑍇।  
𑌸 𑌚 𑌤𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌠𑌤𑌿 𑌵𑍈𑌕𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌠𑍇 𑌯𑌾𑌵𑌦𑍍𑌵𑍈 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌣𑍋 𑌵𑌯𑌃॥௧௪॥  
  
𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌂 𑌪𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌮𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇---  
𑌶𑌙𑍍𑌖𑍋𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌾𑌰𑍇 𑌨𑌰𑌃 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌦𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌟𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌂 𑌗𑌦𑌾𑌧𑌰𑌮𑍍॥௩௫॥  
𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌕𑌲𑌾𑌂 𑌨𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌹𑌤𑌿 𑌷𑍋𑌡𑌶𑍀𑌮𑍍।  
𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌷𑍁 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌲𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌂 𑌯𑍋 𑌦𑌦𑌾𑌤𑌿 𑌨𑍃𑌪𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌮॥௩௬॥  
𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌕𑌲𑌾𑌂 𑌨𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌹𑌤𑌿 𑌷𑍋𑌡𑌶𑍀𑌮𑍍।  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌭𑌾𑌸𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍇 𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌗𑍍𑌰𑌹𑌣𑍇 𑌚𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌸𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌯𑍋𑌃॥௩௭॥

82aac865d2.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between budhaḥ and śukraḥ in śravaṇaḥ makaraḥ, center-to-center separation 0°41′09.45″.
82aac865d2.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°41′09.45″, 0°41′02.09″ apart, disc-to-disc. budhaḥ at śravaṇaḥ-4 makaraḥ (latitude 2°00′23.81″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -1.28, elongation 5°47′39.57″ E). śukraḥ at śravaṇaḥ-4 makaraḥ (latitude 1°19′14.36″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -3.91, elongation 5°35′40.43″ E). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here budhaḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śukraḥ is taken as jayI over budhaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

82b35ee28b.d: Anadhyayana on account of pūrṇimā. Several tithis in a month are nitya-anadhyayana days, including prathamā, aṣṭamī, chaturdaśī, amāvāsyā and pūrṇimā. Manu has said that performing adhyayana on these days destroys the Guru (Amavasya), Shishya (Chaturdashi) and the vīrya of the brahma (vēda) itself (Ashtami/Purnima). Similarly, Jabali Rishi has said that Adhyayana on prathama hurts the buddhi while adhyayana on chaturdaśī hurts the brahma (vēda) itself!

𑌹𑌾𑌰𑍀𑌤𑌃—

𑌅𑌮𑌾𑌵𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌗𑍁𑌰𑍁𑌂 𑌹𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌶𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌹𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌦𑌶𑍀।  
𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑌾𑌪𑍌𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌮𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑌰𑌿𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌜𑌯𑍇𑌦𑌿𑌤𑌿॥  
𑌯𑌾𑌜𑍍𑌞𑌵𑌲𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌯𑌃—  
𑌪𑌞𑍍𑌚𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌅𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍁𑌸𑍂𑌤𑌕𑍇।

83715820de.d: It is said in Vishnu Purāṇam that when Amavasya overlaps with one of nine nakshatras---Anuradha, Vishakha, Swati, Pushya, Ardra, Punarvasu, Shravishtha, Purvaproshthapada, or Shatabhishak---it is sacred even for Devas. For instance, Shraaddha done on an Amavasya joined with Anuradha, Vishakha, Swati keeps the pitrs satisfied for eight years. Likewise, on Pushya, Ardra and Punarvasu, the pitrs are satisfied for twelve years. amāvāsyā of āśvayuja month.
83715820de.s:
𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇---  
𑌅𑌮𑌾𑌵𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌯𑌦𑌾 𑌮𑍈𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌵𑌿𑌶𑌾𑌖𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌤𑌿𑌯𑍋𑌗𑌿𑌨𑍀।  
𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌧𑍇 𑌪𑌿𑌤𑍃𑌗𑌣𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍃𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌮𑌵𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌨𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌵𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌷𑌿𑌕𑍀𑌮𑍍॥  
𑌅𑌮𑌾𑌵𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌯𑌦𑌾 𑌪𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌯𑍇 𑌰𑍌𑌦𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌽𑌥𑌃 𑌪𑍁𑌨𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌸𑍌।  
𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌶𑌾𑌬𑍍𑌦𑌂 𑌤𑌦𑌾 𑌤𑍃𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌯𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌪𑌿𑌤𑌰𑍋𑌽𑌰𑍍𑌚𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌃॥  
𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌵𑌾𑌜𑍈𑌕𑌪𑌾𑌦𑍃𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇 𑌪𑌿𑌤𑍄𑌣𑌾𑌂 𑌤𑍃𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌮𑌿𑌚𑍍𑌛𑌤𑌾𑌮𑍍।  
𑌵𑌾𑌰𑍁𑌣𑍇 𑌚𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌯𑌮𑌾𑌵𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌮𑌪𑌿 𑌦𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌲𑌭𑌾।  
𑌨𑌵𑌸𑍍𑌵𑍃𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇𑌷𑍍𑌵𑌮𑌾𑌵𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌯𑌦𑍈𑌤𑍇𑌷𑍍𑌵𑌵𑌨𑍀𑌪𑌤𑍇॥

843428053a.d:
Coming from Brahma's Kamandalu, Pushkara Raja resides in different rivers, along with 3.5 crore tirthas, following the Sankranti of Guru, for twelve days at the beginning of the Sankranti (ādya puṣkaram) and at the end of the year (preceding transition to the next rāśī, antya puṣkaram), and for two muhurtas during mid-day, every day, during the entire year.
As Guru is about to leave vr̥ṣabhaḥ, puṣkararāja's residence in the narmadā river draws to a close.
843428053a.s:
𑌮𑍇𑌷𑍇 𑌚 𑌗𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌾 𑌵𑍃𑌷𑌭𑍇 𑌚 𑌨𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌦𑌾 𑌯𑍁𑌗𑍍𑌮𑍇 𑌚 𑌵𑌾𑌣𑍀 𑌯𑌮𑍁𑌨𑌾 𑌕𑍁𑌲𑍀𑌰𑍇  
𑌗𑍋𑌦𑌾𑌵𑌰𑍀 𑌸𑌿𑌂𑌹𑌗𑌤𑍇 𑌚 𑌕𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌤𑍇 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌗𑍁𑌰𑍌 𑌚 𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌾।  
𑌕𑌾𑌵𑍇𑌰𑍀 𑌤𑍌𑌲𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌅𑌲𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌮𑍍𑌰𑌪𑌰𑍍𑌣𑍀 𑌚𑌾𑌪𑍇 𑌚 𑌸𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌧𑍁 𑌮𑌕𑌰𑍇 𑌚 𑌭𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌾  
𑌘𑌟𑍇 𑌗𑍁𑌰𑍌 𑌭𑍀𑌮𑌰𑌥𑍀 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌣𑍀𑌤𑌾 𑌮𑍀𑌨𑍇 𑌗𑌤𑍇 𑌪𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌕𑌰𑌮𑌾𑌹𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌃॥  
𑌯𑌦𑌾 𑌰𑌾𑌶𑌿-𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌵𑍇𑌶𑌃 𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌦𑌾 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌭𑍃𑌤𑌿 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌦𑌾।  
𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌶𑌾𑌹𑌮𑌿𑌤𑍇 𑌕𑌾𑌲𑍇 𑌵𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌤𑍁 𑌮𑌮𑌾𑌽𑌽𑌜𑍍𑌞𑌯𑌾॥  
𑌆𑌵𑌤𑍍𑌸𑌰𑌂 𑌤𑍁 𑌵𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌮𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌨𑍇 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌮𑍁𑌹𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌕𑌮𑍍।  
𑌅𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌶 𑌵𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌚 𑌯𑌥𑌾𑌸𑍁𑌖𑌮𑍍॥

844d96b48a.d: On this navamī day, Bhagavan Mahavishnu killed a Daitya named Kūṣmāṇḍa. The creepers of pumpkin gourd grew from the hairs of that Daitya. Perform danam of kūṣmāṇḍa, i.e. pumpkin, to obtain merits.
844d96b48a.s:
𑌨𑌾𑌰𑌦 𑌉𑌵𑌾𑌚---  
𑌶𑍃𑌣𑍁 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌵𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑌿 𑌮𑌾𑌹𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌨𑌾𑌶𑌨𑌮𑍍।  
𑌅𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌾 𑌨𑌵𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌯𑌦𑍍𑌗𑍋𑌪𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌚 𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌪𑍇॥௧॥  
𑌤𑌦𑌹𑌂 𑌤𑍇 𑌸𑌮𑌗𑍍𑌰𑌂 𑌚 𑌕𑌥𑌯𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌯𑍇 𑌤𑌪𑍋𑌧𑌨।  
𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌕𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌤𑍁 𑌶𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌨𑌵𑌮𑍀𑌤𑌿𑌥𑌿𑌃॥௨॥  
𑌅𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌯𑌾 𑌸𑌾 𑌤𑍁 𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌪𑍍𑌰𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌾 𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌸𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌮𑍁𑌨𑌿𑌪𑍁𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌵𑍈𑌃।  
𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌕𑌰𑌣𑌂 𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌚𑍍𑌛𑍃𑌣𑍁𑌧𑍍𑌵𑌂 𑌹𑌰𑌿𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌯𑌮𑍍॥௩॥  
𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌮𑍇 𑌮𑍁𑌹𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌚𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌥𑌾𑌯 𑌚𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌯𑍇𑌦𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌮𑌨𑍋 𑌹𑌿𑌤𑌮𑍍।  
𑌕𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌨𑌿𑌮𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌕𑌂 𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌮 𑌪𑍂𑌜𑌯𑍇𑌦𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌤𑌾𑌃॥௪॥  
𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌪𑍂𑌜𑌾𑌂 𑌵𑌿𑌧𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌽𑌽𑌦𑍌 𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌪𑌞𑍍𑌚𑍋𑌪𑌚𑌾𑌰𑌕𑍈𑌃।  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌦𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌨𑍈𑌵𑍇𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌨𑌂 𑌸𑌲𑌵𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌕𑌮𑍍॥௫॥  
𑌜𑍀𑌰𑌕𑌂 𑌨𑌾𑌗𑌰𑌂 𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌮𑌰𑌿𑌚𑌂 𑌦𑌾𑌡𑌿𑌮𑌂 𑌤𑌥𑌾।  
𑌨𑌾𑌰𑌿𑌕𑍇𑌲𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌚𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌕𑍂𑌷𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌣𑍍𑌡𑌕𑌾𑌞𑍍𑌚𑌨𑍀𑌯𑍁𑌤𑌮𑍍॥௬॥  
𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌕𑌲𑍍𑌪𑍍𑌯 𑌦𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌚𑍍𑌛𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌯𑌤𑌾𑌮𑌿𑌤𑌿 𑌚𑌾𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌯𑌃।  
𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌶𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌤𑍋𑌷𑌯𑍇𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌨𑌮𑌸𑍍𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍇𑌣 𑌵𑌾 𑌪𑍁𑌨𑌃॥௭॥  
𑌸𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌗𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍇 𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍇 𑌤𑍁𑌲𑌾𑌦𑌾𑌨𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌫𑌲𑌮𑍍।  
𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌲𑌭𑌤𑍇 𑌮𑌰𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌕𑍂𑌷𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌣𑍍𑌡𑌦𑌾𑌨𑌤𑌃॥௮॥  
𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌪𑌾𑌤𑌕𑌯𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍋𑌽𑌪𑌿 𑌤𑌦𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍋 𑌚𑍋𑌪𑌪𑌾𑌤𑌕𑍈𑌃।  
𑌨𑌰𑍋 𑌵𑌿𑌶𑍁𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌮𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍋 𑌹𑌿 𑌯𑌮𑌲𑍋𑌕𑌂 𑌨 𑌪𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌤𑌿॥௯॥  
𑌕𑍂𑌷𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌣𑍍𑌡𑌦𑌾𑌨𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌰𑌃 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌲𑍋𑌕𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌜𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌵𑍈।  
𑌸𑍍𑌵𑍇𑌚𑍍𑌛𑌯𑌾 𑌪𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌟𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌭𑍋𑌗𑌰𑌤𑌾 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌜॥௧௦॥  
𑌶𑍌𑌨𑌕 𑌉𑌵𑌾𑌚---  
𑌭𑍂𑌲𑍋𑌕𑍇 𑌕𑍇𑌨 𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌂 𑌹𑌿 𑌵𑌦 𑌮𑌹𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌮𑍁𑌨𑍀𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌰।  
𑌦𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌕𑍂𑌷𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌣𑍍𑌡𑌕𑌮𑌯𑌂 𑌯𑍇𑌨 𑌕𑍌𑌤𑍂𑌹𑌲𑌂 𑌹𑌿 𑌮𑍇॥௧௧॥  
𑌨𑌾𑌰𑌦 𑌉𑌵𑌾𑌚---  
𑌅𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍇𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌗𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌮𑍋 𑌯𑌾𑌮𑍁𑌨𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌗𑌿𑌰𑍇𑌰𑌧𑌃।  
𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌸𑍁𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌣𑍋 𑌰𑌾𑌮𑌶𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌽𑌸𑍌 𑌲𑍋𑌕𑌵𑌿𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍁𑌤𑌃॥௧௨॥  
𑌤𑍇𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌧𑌨𑌂 𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌗𑌰𑍍𑌜𑌿𑌤𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌚𑍁𑌰𑌂 𑌕𑌿𑌲।  
𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌪𑌰𑍋𑌦𑌾𑌤𑌾 𑌵𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌕𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌸𑌮𑍁𑌪𑌾𑌗𑌤𑌃॥௧௩॥  
𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌪𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍌 𑌤𑍁 𑌸𑌞𑍍𑌜𑌾𑌤𑍌 𑌨𑌾𑌮𑍍𑌨𑌾 𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌧𑌨𑌞𑍍𑌜𑌯𑍌।  
𑌤𑌯𑍋𑌰𑍍𑌮𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌵𑌹𑌂 𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌜𑌗𑌾𑌮 𑌤𑌪𑌸𑍇 𑌵𑌨𑌮𑍍॥௧௪॥  
𑌤𑌪𑌃 𑌕𑍍𑌲𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌶𑌰𑍀𑌰𑍋𑌽𑌸𑍌 𑌵𑌾𑌸𑍁𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌮𑌨𑌃 𑌸𑌦𑌾।  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌵𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌵𑍈𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌵𑌂 𑌸𑍍𑌥𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌗𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌨 𑌶𑍋𑌚𑌤𑌿॥௧௫॥  
𑌤𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌸𑍁𑌤𑍌 𑌤𑍌 𑌤𑍁 𑌕𑌾𑌲𑍇 𑌤𑌰𑍁𑌣𑌾𑌤𑌾𑌂 𑌗𑌤𑍌।  
𑌵𑌾𑌰𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌰𑌤𑌿𑌸𑌂𑌸𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍌 𑌮𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌪𑌾𑌨𑌰𑌤𑍌 𑌸𑌦𑌾॥௧௬॥  
𑌨 𑌶𑍃𑌣𑍍𑌵𑌤𑍇 𑌵𑌚𑌃 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌂 𑌵𑍃𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌂 𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌤𑌾𑌵𑍁𑌭𑍌।  
𑌪𑌰𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌭𑍍𑌯𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌦𑌦𑌤𑍁𑌃 𑌸𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌂 𑌚 𑌶𑌤𑌂 𑌤𑌥𑌾॥௧௭॥  
𑌏𑌵𑌂 𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌯𑌂 𑌨𑍀𑌤𑌂 𑌤𑌾𑌭𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌣𑌸𑍁𑌖𑌾𑌯 𑌵𑍈  
𑌮𑌲𑍍𑌲𑍌 𑌚𑌾𑌣𑍂𑌰𑌶𑍈𑌲𑍂𑌷𑍌 𑌵𑍇𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌤𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌯𑌾𑌵𑍁𑌭𑍌॥௧௮॥  
𑌅𑌪𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍇 𑌤𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌨𑌂 𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌂 𑌭𑍁𑌵𑌿 𑌬𑍀𑌜𑌮𑌿𑌵𑍋𑌷𑌰𑍇।  
𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌯𑌾𑌦𑍁𑌭𑍌 𑌭𑍂𑌤𑍌 𑌚𑍌𑌰𑌮𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌗𑌾𑌨𑍁𑌸𑌾𑌰𑌿𑌣𑍌॥௧௯॥  
𑌰𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍌 𑌤𑍁 𑌕𑍋𑌟𑌪𑌾𑌲𑍇𑌨 𑌧𑍃𑌤𑌾 𑌰𑌾𑌜𑍍𑌞𑌾 𑌚 𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌿𑌤𑍌।  
𑌵𑌨𑌂 𑌗𑌤𑍌 𑌤𑍁 𑌤𑍌 𑌸𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌧𑌮𑌧𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌨𑌿𑌰𑌤𑍌 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌜𑍌॥௨௦॥  
𑌮𑌾𑌂𑌸𑌾𑌹𑌾𑌰𑌿𑌣𑍌 𑌸𑌞𑍍𑌜𑌾𑌤𑍌 𑌸𑌿𑌂𑌹𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌮𑍁𑌪𑌾𑌗𑌤𑍌।  
𑌏𑌕𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌦𑌿𑌵𑌸𑍇 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑍌 𑌯𑌮𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌂 𑌗𑌤𑍌॥௨௧॥  
𑌯𑌮𑌦𑍂𑌤𑍌 𑌤𑌦𑌾 𑌵𑌾𑌕𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌕𑌾 𑌶𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌃 𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌯𑌤𑍇 𑌵𑌿𑌭𑍋।  
𑌕𑌿𑌙𑍍𑌕𑌰𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌵𑌚𑌃 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌤𑌦𑌾 𑌵𑍈𑌵𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌤𑍋 𑌯𑌮𑌃॥௨௨॥  
𑌚𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌗𑍁𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌲𑍇𑌖𑌨𑍀𑌯𑌂 𑌨𑌰𑌾𑌣𑌾𑌂 𑌚 𑌶𑍁𑌭𑌾𑌶𑍁𑌭𑌮𑍍।  
𑌏𑌕𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌕𑍍𑌰𑍋𑌧𑌤𑌾𑌮𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌃 𑌏𑌤𑍌 𑌕𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌿𑌪𑌾𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌹𑌮𑍍॥௨௩॥  
𑌚𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌗𑍁𑌪𑍍𑌤𑍋𑌽𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌵𑍀𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌕𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌕𑌿𑌙𑍍𑌕𑌰𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌶𑍂𑌲𑌧𑌾𑌰𑌿𑌣𑌃।  
𑌏𑌕𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌨𑍀𑌯𑌤𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌗𑍇 𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌭𑍋𑌗𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌶𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌤𑌾𑌃॥௨௪॥  
𑌅𑌪𑌰𑍋 𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌿𑌪𑍍𑌯𑌤𑌾𑌂 𑌦𑍂𑌤𑌾 𑌨𑌰𑌕𑍇 𑌯𑌾𑌤𑌨𑌾𑌕𑍁𑌲𑍇।  
𑌚𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌗𑍁𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌵𑌚𑌃 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌤𑌦𑌾 𑌦𑍂𑌤𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌯𑌂𑌵𑌦𑌃॥௨௫॥  
𑌨𑍀𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌧𑌨𑌞𑍍𑌜𑌯𑌂 𑌤𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌃 𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌗𑌮𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌗𑌮𑍁𑌪𑌾𑌗𑌤𑌃।  
𑌅𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌣𑌂 𑌗𑍃𑌹𑍀𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌶𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌕𑌮𑍍॥௨௬॥  
𑌨𑌰𑌕𑍇𑌽𑌪𑌾𑌤𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌰𑍁𑌦𑍍𑌧𑍋 𑌭𑍁𑌙𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌵 𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌕𑍃𑌤𑌂 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌜।  
𑌧𑌨𑌞𑍍𑌜𑌯𑍋 𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌜𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌗𑍇 𑌪𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌵𑍈𑌚𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌮𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌵𑌾𑌨𑍍॥௨௭॥  
𑌅𑌪𑍍𑌸𑌰𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌤𑌦𑌾𑌗𑌤𑍍𑌯 𑌉𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌮𑍁𑌨𑍇।  
𑌪𑌾𑌰𑌿𑌜𑌾𑌤𑌕𑍃𑌤𑌾𑌂 𑌮𑌾𑌲𑌾𑌂 𑌶𑌿𑌰𑌸𑌿 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌿𑌪𑌨𑍍𑌮𑍁𑌦𑌾॥௨௮॥  
𑌇𑌤𑌿 𑌦𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌟𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌤𑌦𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌗𑌮𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌗𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌶𑍌𑌨𑌕।  
𑌪𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌵𑌾𑌨𑍍 𑌯𑌮𑌦𑍂𑌤𑌂 𑌚 𑌤𑌦𑌾 𑌸𑌕𑌰𑍁𑌣𑌂 𑌵𑌚𑌃॥௨௯॥  
𑌧𑌨𑌞𑍍𑌜𑌯 𑌉𑌵𑌾𑌚---  
𑌏𑌕𑌾 𑌮𑌾𑌤𑌾 𑌪𑌿𑌤𑌾 𑌚𑍈𑌕𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌭𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌜𑌾𑌤𑍌 𑌸𑌹𑍋𑌦𑌰𑍌।  
𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌮𑍇𑌵 𑌕𑍃𑌤𑌂 𑌤𑌾𑌭𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌨 𑌵𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌾 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌣𑌃॥௩௦॥  
𑌏𑌕𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌦𑌿𑌵𑌸𑍇 𑌦𑍂𑌤 𑌮𑍃𑌤𑍌 𑌯𑌮𑌪𑍁𑌰𑍀𑌂 𑌗𑌤𑍌।  
𑌕𑌥𑌂 𑌸 𑌨𑌰𑌕𑍇 𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌿𑌪𑍍𑌤𑍋 𑌮𑌮 𑌜𑍍𑌯𑍇𑌷𑍍𑌠𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌯𑌂𑌵𑌦॥௩௧॥  
𑌮𑌮 𑌭𑌾𑌵𑍀 𑌕𑌥𑌂 𑌨𑌾𑌥 𑌸𑌂𑌶𑌯𑍋𑌽𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌮।  
𑌯𑌮𑌦𑍂𑌤 𑌉𑌵𑌾𑌚---  
𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌸𑌾 𑌮𑌾𑌤𑌾 𑌪𑌿𑌤𑌾 𑌭𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌤𑌾 𑌪𑌿𑌤𑍃𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌧𑌨𑌞𑍍𑌜𑌯।  
𑌅𑌦𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌜𑌾 𑌸𑌂𑌜𑍍𑌞𑌾 𑌜𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌮𑍋𑌪𑌭𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌯𑍇॥௩௨॥  
𑌯𑌥𑌾 𑌕𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌗𑌤𑍇 𑌸𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌯𑍇 𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌶𑍁𑌨𑍀𑌨𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑌮𑌾𑌗𑌮𑌃।  
𑌪𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌭𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌤𑍃𑌪𑌿𑌤𑍄𑌣𑌾𑌂 𑌚 𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌭𑌵𑌤𑌿 𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌮𑌃॥௩௩॥  
𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌚𑍍𑌚𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌾 𑌨 𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌜 𑌮𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌗 𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌵𑍈।  
𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌵𑌾𑌂𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌂 𑌸𑍁𑌕𑍃𑌤𑌿𑌨𑌾𑌂 𑌲𑍋𑌕𑌂 𑌯𑌾𑌸𑌿 𑌨𑌮𑍋𑌽𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌤𑍇॥௩௪॥  
𑌕𑍇𑌨 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑍇𑌨 𑌮𑌾𑌂 𑌦𑍂𑌤 𑌨𑌯𑌸𑌿 𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌂 𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌪𑌮𑍍।  
𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌠𑌾 𑌮𑌤𑍍𑌪𑌰𑍋 𑌨𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌯𑍋 𑌭𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌤𑌿 𑌧𑌰𑌾𑌤𑌲𑍇॥௩௫॥  
𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌤𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌚𑌨𑌂 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌯𑌮𑌦𑍂𑌤𑍋𑌽𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌵𑍀𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌚𑌃।  
𑌪𑌾𑌠𑌕𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌗𑍇𑌨 𑌗𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌂 𑌯𑌮𑍁𑌨𑌾𑌂 𑌕𑌿𑌲।  
𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌸𑍀 𑌚 𑌗𑍁𑌰𑍋𑌰𑍍𑌗𑍃𑌹𑍍𑌯 𑌕𑍁𑌶𑌾𑌂𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌸𑌮𑌿𑌧𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌥𑌾॥௩௬॥  
𑌆𑌚𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌜𑍍𑌞𑌯𑌾 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌮𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌜𑍇 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌤𑌃 𑌕𑍃𑌤𑌂 𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌹𑌮𑍍।  
𑌨𑌿𑌯𑌮𑌂 𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌕𑍃𑌤𑌂 𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌸𑌞𑍍𑌜𑌾𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌮𑌹𑌤𑍍𑌫𑌲𑌮𑍍॥௩௭॥  
𑌏𑌕𑍇𑌨 𑌮𑌜𑍍𑌜𑍇𑌨𑌨𑌾𑌶𑍁 𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌮𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍋𑌽𑌸𑌿 𑌜𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌨𑌃।  
𑌮𑌜𑍍𑌜𑌨𑍇𑌨 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌤𑍀𑌯𑍇𑌨 𑌅𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌯𑌂 𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌗𑌮𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌨𑍁𑌹𑌿॥௩௮॥  
𑌨𑌰𑌕𑍇 𑌚 𑌤𑌵 𑌭𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌤𑌾 𑌸𑌹𑌤𑌾𑌂 𑌯𑌮𑌯𑌾𑌤𑌨𑌾𑌮𑍍।  
𑌇𑌤𑌿 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌵𑌚𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌭𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌤𑍃𑌗𑍌𑌰𑌵𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌤𑌃॥௩௯॥  
𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌦𑍂𑌤 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌣𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌹𑌂 𑌮𑍈𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌂 𑌸𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌪𑌦𑍀𑌂 𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌰𑌨𑍍।  
𑌨𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌗𑌮𑍋 𑌨𑌰𑌕𑌾𑌦𑍍 𑌦𑍂𑌤 𑌭𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌮𑍇 𑌜𑌾𑌯𑌤𑍇 𑌕𑌥𑌮𑍍॥௪௦॥  
𑌯𑌥𑌾𑌽𑌹𑌂 𑌭𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌤𑍃𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌗𑍇𑌨 𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌗𑌂 𑌯𑌾𑌮𑌿 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌯𑌂𑌵𑌦।  
𑌨 𑌹𑌿 𑌭𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌤𑍃𑌸𑌮𑍋 𑌬𑌨𑍍𑌧𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌨 𑌹𑌿 𑌭𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌤𑍃𑌸𑌮𑌃 𑌸𑌖𑌾॥௪௧॥  
𑌨 𑌹𑌿 𑌭𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌤𑍃𑌸𑌮𑍋 𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌤𑌾 𑌮𑌾𑌤𑍃𑌜𑌾𑌤𑌂 𑌵𑌿𑌶𑍇𑌷𑌤𑌃।  
𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌗𑌂 𑌨𑍇𑌚𑍍𑌛𑍇 𑌵𑌿𑌨𑌾 𑌤𑍇𑌨 𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌮𑍇 𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌨𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍃𑌤𑌿𑌃॥௪௨॥  
𑌯𑌥𑌾 𑌭𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌤𑌾 𑌸𑌮𑍋 𑌯𑍋𑌗𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌮𑍁𑌪𑌾𑌯𑌂 𑌵𑌦𑌸𑍍𑌵 𑌮𑍇।  
𑌇𑌤𑌿 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌵𑌚𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌦𑍂𑌤𑍋𑌽𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌵𑍀𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌤𑌃॥௪௩॥  
𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌜𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌕𑍃𑌤𑌂 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌤𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌦𑌾𑌮𑌿 𑌧𑌨𑌞𑍍𑌜𑌯।  
𑌦𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌨𑌵𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌕𑍂𑌷𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌣𑍍𑌡𑌸𑍍𑌯𑍋𑌰𑍍𑌜𑍇𑌶𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑌤𑌿𑌥𑍌 𑌦𑌿𑌨𑍇॥௪௪॥  
𑌸𑌹𑌿𑌰𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌯𑌾 𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌂 𑌸𑌰𑌤𑍍𑌨𑌂 𑌚 𑌸𑌵𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌕𑌮𑍍।  
𑌦𑍇𑌹𑌿 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌚 𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌂 𑌭𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍇 𑌦𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌗𑌿𑌣𑌾𑌮𑌪𑌿॥௪௫॥  
𑌇𑌤𑌿 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌵𑌚𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌦𑍂𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌸𑌾𑌦𑌰𑌮𑍍।  
𑌦𑌦𑍌 𑌭𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍇 𑌚 𑌕𑍂𑌷𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌣𑍍𑌡𑌦𑌾𑌨𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌧𑌨𑌞𑍍𑌜𑌯𑌃॥௪௬॥  
𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌦𑌾𑌨𑍇𑌨 𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍋𑌽𑌪𑌿 𑌨𑌰𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌾𑌗𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌦𑌾।  
𑌭𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾 𑌸𑌹 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌜𑌵𑌰𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌵𑌾𑌨𑍍 𑌵𑍈𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌵𑌂 𑌪𑌦𑌮𑍍॥௪௭॥  
𑌭𑍋𑌗𑍋𑌪𑌭𑍋𑌗𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌪𑌨𑍍𑌨𑍌 𑌯𑌮𑌦𑍂𑌤𑌵𑌿𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌜𑌿𑌤𑍌।  
𑌅𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌪𑌿 𑌤𑍌 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌜𑌵𑌰𑍌 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌶𑍀𑌲𑌸𑍁𑌶𑍀𑌲𑌕𑍌॥௪௮॥  
𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌵𑌭𑍂𑌤𑌾𑌂 𑌵𑍈 𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌾𑌰𑌾𑌧𑌨𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌪𑌰𑍌।  
𑌨𑌵𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌮𑍁𑌦𑍍𑌦𑌿𑌶𑍍𑌯 𑌶𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇 𑌵𑌿𑌚𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌣𑍈𑌃॥௪௯॥  
𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌕𑍇 𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌿 𑌕𑍂𑌷𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌣𑍍𑌡𑌂 𑌸𑌹𑌿𑌰𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌸𑌵𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌕𑌮𑍍।  
𑌕𑍂𑌷𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌣𑍍𑌡𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌚 𑌦𑌾𑌨𑍇𑌨 𑌤𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌕𑍋𑌟𑌿𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍁𑌷𑌾𑌃॥௫௦॥  
𑌏𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌕𑌥𑌿𑌤𑌂 𑌵𑌿𑌪𑍍𑌰 𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌕𑌨𑌵𑌮𑍀𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌮𑍍।  
𑌕𑍂𑌷𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌣𑍍𑌡𑌦𑌾𑌨𑌮𑌾𑌹𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌯𑌦𑍍𑌗𑍀𑌤𑌂 𑌯𑌮𑌦𑍂𑌤𑌕𑍈𑌃॥௫௧॥  
𑌧𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍍𑌯𑍈 𑌚𑍈𑌕𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌣𑌾𑌮𑍇𑌨 𑌅𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌮𑍇𑌧𑌾𑌧𑌿𑌕𑌂 𑌫𑌲𑌮𑍍।  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌦𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌿𑌣𑌾𑌂 𑌤𑍁 𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍁𑌤𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌮𑍇𑌤𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌯𑍋𑌦𑌿𑌤𑌮𑍍॥௫௨॥  
𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌣𑌾𑌨𑍍 𑌸𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌘𑌾𑌂𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌹𑌰𑌿𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌪𑌰𑌾𑌯𑌣𑌾𑌨𑍍।  
𑌭𑍁𑌞𑍍𑌜𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌚𑍈𑌵 𑌯𑍇 𑌵𑌿𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍇𑌷𑌾𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌨𑌂 𑌗𑍁𑌣𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌦𑌮𑍍॥௫௩॥  
𑌧𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌚𑍍𑌛𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑌮𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌯 𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌕𑍇𑌽𑌨𑍍𑌨𑌂 𑌤𑍁 𑌭𑍁𑌜𑍍𑌯𑌤𑍇।  
𑌅𑌨𑍍𑌨𑌸𑌂𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌗𑌜𑌂 𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌂 𑌬𑌹𑍁𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌷𑌂 𑌚 𑌨𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌤𑌿॥௫௪॥  
𑌇𑌤𑌿 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌪𑌦𑍍𑌮𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇 𑌅𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌯𑌨𑌵𑌮𑍀𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌕𑌥𑌾 𑌸𑌮𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌾॥  
  
𑌅𑌥 𑌕𑍂𑌷𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌣𑍍𑌡𑌦𑌾𑌨𑌵𑌿𑌧𑌿𑌃---  
𑌕𑍂𑌷𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌣𑍍𑌡𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌤𑌾𑌯𑍈 𑌨𑌮𑌃 𑌇𑌤𑌿 𑌗𑌨𑍍𑌧𑌪𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌪𑍈𑌃 𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌪𑍂𑌜𑍍𑌯 𑌦𑍇𑌶𑌕𑌾𑌲𑍌 𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌕𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯 𑌅𑌮𑍁𑌕𑌗𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌅𑌮𑍁𑌕𑌶𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌾  
𑌮𑌮 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌹𑌨𑌨𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌸𑌮𑌸𑍍𑌤-𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌯-𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌕-𑌬𑌹𑍁𑌪𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌰-𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀-𑌸𑍌𑌭𑌾𑌗𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑌿-𑌸𑌕𑌲-𑌮𑌨𑍋𑌰𑌥𑌾𑌵𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌿-𑌕𑍂𑌷𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌣𑍍𑌡-  
𑌬𑍀𑌜-𑌸𑌸𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰-𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌖𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌕𑌾𑌬𑍍𑌦-𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌲𑍋𑌕-𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌲𑍋𑌕-𑌰𑍁𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌲𑍋𑌕𑌨𑌿𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌕𑌾𑌮𑌃 𑌅𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌯𑌨𑌵𑌮𑍀-𑌯𑍁𑌗𑌾𑌦𑌿-  
𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌪𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌨𑌿𑌮𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌮𑌿𑌦𑌂 𑌕𑍂𑌷𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌣𑍍𑌡𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌬𑌹𑍁𑌬𑍀𑌜𑌾𑌢𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌘𑍃𑌤𑌪𑍍𑌲𑍁𑌤𑌂 𑌤𑌿𑌲𑌲𑌿𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌂 𑌸𑍁𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌤𑌾𑌮𑍍𑌬𑍂𑌲𑌵𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌯𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌂  
𑌗𑍋𑌧𑍂𑌮𑌰𑌾𑌶𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌥𑌿𑌤𑌂 𑌵𑌨𑌸𑍍𑌪𑌤𑌿𑌦𑍈𑌵𑌤𑌂 𑌦𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌿𑌣𑌾𑌯𑍁𑌤𑌂 𑌯𑌥𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌮𑌗𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌯 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌣𑌾𑌯 𑌦𑌾𑌤𑍁𑌮𑌹𑌮𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌸𑍃𑌜𑍇॥  
𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌹𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌘𑍍𑌨𑌂 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌣𑌾 𑌨𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌿𑌤𑌂 𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾।  
𑌕𑍂𑌷𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌣𑍍𑌡𑌂 𑌬𑌹𑍁𑌬𑍀𑌜𑌾𑌢𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌪𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌪𑍌𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌵𑍃𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌿𑌦𑌮𑍍॥  
𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌵𑍇 𑌨𑌮𑌃॥  
  
𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌕𑍇 𑌶𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑌨𑌵𑌮𑍀 𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌽𑌭𑍂𑌦𑍍 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌪𑌰𑌂 𑌯𑍁𑌗𑌮𑍍।  
𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌽𑌪𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌣𑌗𑌾 𑌗𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌮𑌾𑌦𑍍 𑌦𑌾𑌨𑍋𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌯𑍋𑌃॥௧॥  
𑌅𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌕𑍂𑌷𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌣𑍍𑌡𑌕𑍋 𑌨𑌾𑌮 𑌹𑌤𑍋 𑌦𑍈𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌨𑌾।  
𑌤𑌦𑍍𑌰𑍋𑌮𑌭𑌿𑌃 𑌸𑌮𑍁𑌦𑍍𑌭𑍂𑌤𑌾 𑌵𑌲𑍍𑌲𑍍𑌯𑌃 𑌕𑍂𑌷𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌣𑍍𑌡𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌭𑌵𑌾𑌃॥௨॥  
𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌤𑍍 𑌕𑍂𑌷𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌣𑍍𑌡𑌦𑌾𑌨𑍇𑌨 𑌫𑌲𑌮𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌨𑍋𑌤𑌿 𑌨𑌿𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌿𑌤𑌮𑍍।  
---𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌸𑍍𑌕𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍇 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌤𑍀𑌯𑍇 𑌵𑍈𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌵𑌖𑌣𑍍𑌡𑍇 𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌕𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌮𑌾𑌹𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌮𑍍𑌯𑍇 𑌕𑍂𑌷𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌣𑍍𑌡𑌨𑌵𑌮𑍀𑌤𑍁𑌲𑌸𑍀𑌵𑌿𑌵𑌾𑌹𑌵𑌿𑌧𑌿𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌨𑌂 𑌨𑌾𑌮𑍈𑌕𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌂𑌶𑍋𑌽𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌃

847cde4c7f.d:
When Shravana nakshatra falls on a Monday, it is a special yōgaḥ. In the cyclic rotation of time, along with the bad combinations of grahas and nakshatras that indicate the probability of upcoming difficulties, good combinations that grant benefits in multiples also arise. Among such good combinations are the Amrita Siddhi yogas of certain weekdays and nakshatras. They are Sunday-Hasta, Monday-Mrigashirsha, Tuesday-Ashvini, Wednesday-Anuradha, Thursday-Pushya, Friday-Revati, Saturday-Rohini. Good deeds performed on such yogas become especially strong in protecting and nourishing us.
For instance, in Devi Atharvashirsha, it is said bhaumāśvinyāṁ mahādevī-sannidhau japtvā mahāmr̥tyuṁ tarati, that is, one can cross even mahāmr̥tyu by doing parayanam when Tuesday and Ashvini join.
847cde4c7f.s:
𑌆𑌦𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌗𑍁𑌰𑍁𑌪𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌯𑍋𑌗𑍇 𑌬𑍁𑌧𑌾𑌨𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌧𑌾 𑌶𑌨𑌿𑌰𑍋𑌹𑌿𑌣𑍀 𑌚।  
𑌸𑍋𑌮𑍇 𑌚 𑌸𑍌𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌭𑍃𑌗𑍁𑌰𑍇𑌵𑌤𑍀 𑌚 𑌭𑍌𑌮𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌨𑍀 𑌚𑌾𑌮𑍃𑌤𑌸𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌿𑌯𑍋𑌗𑌾𑌃॥

84a1a70326.b: Observed on Śukla-Prathamā tithi of Āśvayujaḥ (lunar) month (Sūryōdayaḥ/puurvaviddha).

84a2acc4ca.d: When the transit of the Sun (saṅkrānti) happens in the second half of the day (aparāhṇa) and before midnight, the second half of the day form a puṇyakāla for various observances. In addition to 16 ghatikas on either side of the transition, and specific puṇyakālas like ṣaḍaśīti, viṣṇupadī etc., this is also useful, especially in cases where the other puṇyakālas are inconvenient for appropriate performance of rituals such as snāna, dāna, tarpaṇa, etc.

84a6542930.b: Observed on Paurṇamāsī tithi of Kārttikaḥ (lunar) month (Aparāhṇaḥ/vyaapti).
84a6542930.s:
𑌸𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌰𑍇---  
𑌅𑌮𑌾 𑌪𑌾𑌤𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌵𑍈𑌧𑍃𑌤𑌿𑌰𑍇𑌵 𑌚।  
𑌅𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌚𑍈𑌵 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌗𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌲𑌯𑌃॥  
𑌚𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌸𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌯𑍋𑌪𑌰𑌾𑌗𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌗𑌜𑌚𑍍𑌛𑌾𑌯𑌾 𑌤𑌥𑍈𑌵 𑌚।  
𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌣𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌪𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌃 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌕𑌾𑌲𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌕𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌃॥  
𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌰𑌾𑌦𑌯𑍋 𑌮𑌤𑍍𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇 𑌦𑌰𑍍𑌶𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌃---  
𑌆𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌯𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌛𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑌨𑌵𑌮𑍀 𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌕𑍀 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍀 𑌸𑌿𑌤𑌾।  
𑌤𑍃𑌤𑍀𑌯𑌾 𑌚𑍈𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌸𑌿𑌤𑌾 𑌭𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌪𑌦𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌚॥  
𑌫𑌾𑌲𑍍𑌗𑍁𑌨𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌯𑌮𑌾𑌵𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌪𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌯𑍈𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍀 𑌸𑌿𑌤𑌾।  
𑌆𑌷𑌾𑌢𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌪𑌿 𑌦𑌶𑌮𑍀 𑌮𑌾𑌘𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌮𑍀॥  
𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌵𑌣𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌮𑍀 𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌾 𑌤𑌥𑌾𑌽𑌽𑌷𑌾𑌢𑍀 𑌚 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌿𑌮𑌾।  
𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌕𑍀 𑌫𑌾𑌲𑍍𑌗𑍁𑌨𑍀 𑌚𑍈𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍀 𑌜𑍍𑌯𑍈𑌷𑍍𑌠𑍀 𑌪𑌞𑍍𑌚𑌦𑌶𑍀 𑌸𑌿𑌤𑌾॥  
𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌰𑌾𑌦𑌯𑌶𑍍𑌚𑍈𑌤𑍇 𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌯𑌕𑌾𑌰𑌕𑌾𑌃।  
𑌕𑍃𑌤𑌂 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌂 𑌵𑌿𑌧𑌾𑌨𑍇𑌨 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌷𑍁 𑌯𑍁𑌗𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌷𑍁॥  
𑌹𑌾𑌯𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌸𑌾𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌂 𑌪𑌿𑌤𑍄𑌣𑌾𑌂 𑌤𑍃𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌦𑌂 𑌭𑌵𑍇𑌤𑍍।  
𑌆𑌸𑍁 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌜𑌪𑍋 𑌹𑍋𑌮𑌃 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌨𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯 𑌕𑌲𑍍𑌪𑌤𑍇॥  
𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌭𑌾𑌰𑌤𑍇𑌽𑌪𑌿---   
𑌯𑌾 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌯𑍁𑌗𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌤𑌿𑌥𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌸𑍁 𑌮𑌾𑌨𑌵𑌃।  
𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌭𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌚 𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌚 𑌤𑌦𑌨𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌲𑌭𑍇𑌤𑍍॥  
𑌕𑌾𑌲𑌾𑌦𑌰𑍍𑌶𑍇𑌽𑌪𑌿---  
𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌸𑍁 𑌯𑍁𑌗𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌸𑍁 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌃 𑌸𑌲𑌿𑌲𑌾𑌞𑍍𑌜𑌲𑌿𑌃।  
𑌸𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌵𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌷𑌿𑌕𑍀 𑌤𑍃𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌂 𑌪𑌿𑌤𑍄𑌣𑌾𑌮𑌾𑌵𑌹𑍇𑌤𑍍 𑌪𑌰𑌾𑌮𑍍॥  
𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌸𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌬𑍍𑌦𑌿𑌕𑍀 𑌤𑍃𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌂 𑌕𑍃𑌤𑌂 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌂 𑌯𑌥𑌾𑌵𑌿𑌧𑌿।  
𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌦𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌜𑌪𑍋 𑌹𑍋𑌮𑌃 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌨𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯 𑌕𑌲𑍍𑌪𑌤𑍇॥  
𑌪𑍁𑌰𑍁𑌷𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌚𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌮𑌣𑍌 𑌮𑌨𑍁𑌃---  
𑌸𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌗𑍁𑌣𑌿𑌤𑌂 𑌦𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌭𑌵𑍇𑌦𑍍𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌂 𑌯𑍁𑌗𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌷𑍁।  
𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌮 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌕𑌂 𑌚𑍈𑌵 𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌰𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌷𑍁॥

84be232db0.b: Observed on Śukla-Saptamī tithi of Āśvayujaḥ (lunar) month (Aparāhṇaḥ/vyaapti). The event occurred in 4162 (Kali era).
84be232db0.d: Śrīkaṇṭha, son of Śivasāmbapaṇḍita, known by the appellation Parāśiva (Paramaśiva) (after initiation) who remained in the caves of the mountain since initiation governed the Pīṭha for twenty-one years and having placed poet Somaka’s son, Sūrya, in his place, He attained siddhi in the night of saptami of the bright fortnight in the Aśvini month of the year Śārvari. This preceptor Paramaśivendra stayed in the caves of Sahya mountain adhering to the “mode of python” (ajagaravṛtti), restored to by the disciple named Bodhendra, attained siddhi in the Sahya mountain itself.
84be232db0.s:
𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌕𑌣𑍍𑌠𑌃 𑌶𑌿𑌵𑌸𑌾𑌮𑍍𑌬𑌪𑌣𑍍𑌡𑌿𑌤𑌸𑍁𑌤𑌃 𑌸𑍈𑌕𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑌮𑌾 𑌵𑌿𑌂𑌶𑌤𑌿𑌂  
𑌬𑌿𑌭𑍍𑌰𑌤𑍍 𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌪𑌦𑍇 𑌨𑌿𑌵𑍇𑌶𑍍𑌯 𑌸𑍁𑌕𑌵𑌿𑌂 𑌸𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌮𑌜𑌂 𑌸𑍋𑌮𑌕𑌮𑍍।  
𑌶𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌨𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌮𑍀𑌨𑌿𑌶𑌿 𑌗𑌤𑌃 𑌸𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌿𑌂 𑌸 𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇 𑌸𑌿𑌤𑍇  
𑌸𑌨𑍍𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌸𑌾𑌤𑍍 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌭𑍃𑌤𑌿 𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌿𑌤𑌿𑌧𑍍𑌰-𑌵𑌿𑌵𑌰-𑌸𑍍𑌥𑌾𑌯𑍀 𑌪𑌰𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌃 𑌶𑌿𑌵𑌃॥௮௮॥  
—𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌶𑍍𑌲𑍋𑌕𑌮𑌞𑍍𑌜𑌰𑍀

84eed89b8c.b: Observed on Śukla-Pañcamī tithi of Mārgaśīrṣaḥ (lunar) month (Sūryōdayaḥ/puurvaviddha).
84eed89b8c.d: Widely celebrated in North India, Ayodhya etc., the vivāha dina of Sita–Rama.

84fe129f13.d:
The celestial wedding of Bhagavan Srinivasa and Devi Padmavati is a grand festival held annually in the month of Vaishakha. The beautifully adorned Parinayotsavam Mandapam, set amidst the Narayanagiri gardens, serves as the enchanting venue for this three-day event, celebrated under the moonlit sky. The festivities unfold on the auspicious days of Navami, Dashami, and Ekadashi in the month of Vaishakha, featuring Sri Malayappaswami, Shri Venkateshwara's festival deity. Each day, he makes a grand entrance on different Vahanas: the Gaja (elephant), Ashva (horse), and Garuda (eagle), while Devi-s Sridevi and Bhudevi grace the event on separate palanquins.

Following the wedding rituals at the Parinayotsava Mandapam, a traditional 'Koluvu' gathering takes place, filled with the recitation of Vedic hymns and devotional songs. Bhagavan, accompanied by Sridevi and Bhudevi, then majestically returns to the temple.

Each day's festivities are marked by unique traditional rituals. On the first day, the arrival of Bhagavan Malayappa Swami on the celestial Gaja Vahanam, along with his consorts on their palanquins, is a sight to behold. The traditional wedding ceremony is conducted, where Bhagavan is seated in the ornately decorated Parinaya Mandapam, with his consorts positioned opposite him.

The ceremony includes several traditional rituals such as Edurukolu (mutual reception), Pula Bantata (game of flower balls), and Vastra Dharanam (offering of new clothes). These customs are observed over all three days. The grand finale of the divine marriage is marked by a spectacular display of fireworks, adding to the ceremony's splendor. The event concludes with a procession where Bhagavan Malayappa Swami, along with Devi-s Sridevi and Bhudevi, return to the main temple.

851be56393.d: Aṅgārakaḥ sets into combustion (astamayaH), heading prāk (east), on 2028-Jan-06 07:44. At this moment aṅgārakaḥ is at uttarāṣāḍhā-4 makaraḥ (latitude 1°06′37.71″ S, moving r̥ju (direct)), magnitude +1.17, elongation 16°40′04.92″ E of the Sun. 85e78db3af.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between śaniḥ and śukraḥ in uttaraprōṣṭhapadā mīnaḥ, center-to-center separation 0°54′41.81″.
85e78db3af.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°54′41.81″, 0°54′29.04″ apart, disc-to-disc. śaniḥ at uttaraprōṣṭhapadā-2 mīnaḥ (latitude 2°07′32.83″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude +0.97, elongation 14°48′02.12″ E). śukraḥ at uttaraprōṣṭhapadā-2 mīnaḥ (latitude 1°12′51.03″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -3.90, elongation 14°41′58.75″ E). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here śaniḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śaniḥ is taken as jayI over śukraḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.
85e78db3af.s:
𑌭𑌾𑌵𑌾𑌭𑌾𑌵𑌾𑌯 𑌲𑍋𑌕𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌂 𑌕𑌲𑍍𑌪𑌨𑍇𑌯𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌦𑌰𑍍𑌶𑌿𑌤𑌾।  
𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌮𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌗𑌗𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌯𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑍇𑌤𑍇 𑌦𑍂𑌰𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌯𑍋𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌮𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌃॥  
--𑌸𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌸𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍇  
  
𑌷𑌣𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌂 𑌗𑍍𑌰𑌹𑌭𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌨𑌭𑌂 𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌜 𑌶𑍁𑌭𑍇 𑌯𑍌𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌂 𑌤𑌥𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌪𑌾𑌤𑌭𑌮𑍍।  
--𑌮𑍁𑌹𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌚𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌮𑌣𑍌 (𑌨𑌾𑌰𑌦𑌸𑌂𑌹𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌨𑍁𑌸𑌾𑌰𑍇𑌣)

85f623791f.s:
𑌸𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌰𑍇---  
𑌅𑌮𑌾 𑌪𑌾𑌤𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌵𑍈𑌧𑍃𑌤𑌿𑌰𑍇𑌵 𑌚।  
𑌅𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌚𑍈𑌵 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌗𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌲𑌯𑌃॥  
𑌚𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌸𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌯𑍋𑌪𑌰𑌾𑌗𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌗𑌜𑌚𑍍𑌛𑌾𑌯𑌾 𑌤𑌥𑍈𑌵 𑌚।  
𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌣𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌪𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌃 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌕𑌾𑌲𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌕𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌃॥  
𑌅𑌥𑌾𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑌾𑌃। 𑌤𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌃 𑌮𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌗𑌶𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌷𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌯𑌾𑌪𑌰𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌾𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌃 - 𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌚 𑌶𑍌𑌨𑌕𑌃---  
𑌹𑍇𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌶𑌿𑌶𑌿𑌰𑌯𑍋𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌾𑌮𑌪𑌰𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌾𑌣𑌾𑌮𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌮𑍀𑌷𑍍𑌵𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑌾𑌃 𑌇𑌤𑌿।  
𑌅𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌵𑌿𑌶𑍇𑌷𑌮𑌾𑌹 𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌃---  
𑌅𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌰𑍋𑌽𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌮𑍍𑌯𑍋𑌽𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍇𑌦𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑍌𑌷𑍍𑌠𑌪𑌦𑍇 𑌹𑍇𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌶𑌿𑌶𑌿𑌰𑌯𑍋𑌰𑌪𑌰𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇𑌷𑍁 𑌇𑌤𑌿। 𑌅𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌃 - 𑌨𑌵𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌃, 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍇𑌦𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌃 - 𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌃।  
𑌕𑌾𑌲𑌾𑌦𑌰𑍍𑌶𑍇𑌽𑌪𑌿---  
𑌮𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌗𑌶𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌷𑍇 𑌚 𑌪𑍌𑌷𑍇 𑌚 𑌮𑌾𑌘𑍇 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑍌𑌷𑍍𑌠𑍇 𑌚 𑌫𑌾𑌲𑍍𑌗𑍁𑌨𑍇।  
𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇𑌷𑍁 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍇𑌦𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌰𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌤𑌥𑌾𑌽𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌮𑍀।  
𑌇𑌤𑌿 𑌤𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌰𑍋𑌽𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌸𑍁 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌂 𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍀𑌤 𑌪𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌣𑌮𑍍।  
𑌆𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌲𑌾𑌯𑌨𑌃---  
𑌹𑍇𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌶𑌿𑌶𑌿𑌰𑌰𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑍋𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌾𑌮𑌪𑌿 𑌸𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌮𑍈𑌃।  
𑌸𑌮𑌰𑍍𑌥𑍈𑌰𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑌾 𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌮𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌮𑍀𑌷𑍁 𑌚।   
𑌏𑌕𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌹𑌿 𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌶𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍇𑌨 𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌗𑍃𑌹𑍍𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌮𑌨𑌾 𑌇𑌤𑌿।  
𑌬𑍋𑌧𑌾𑌯𑌨𑍋𑌽𑌪𑌿---  
𑌉𑌪𑌰𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌾𑌨𑍍 𑌮𑌾𑌘𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑍌𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌮𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌅𑌪𑌰𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌨𑌵𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑌿𑌤𑌿 𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌯𑍇𑌤𑌾𑌪𑌿 𑌵𑌾𑌽𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑍇𑌵 𑌇𑌤𑌿।

863db604f7.b: Observed on Śukla-Tr̥tīyā tithi of Vaiśākhaḥ (lunar) month (Pradōṣaḥ/paraviddha).
863db604f7.d: Jayanti of Parashurama, as given in Vrata Raja and Lakshmi Narayana Samhita.
863db604f7.s:
𑌅𑌵𑌤𑌾𑌰𑌦𑌿𑌨𑍇 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑍇 𑌹𑌰𑌿𑌮𑍁𑌦𑍍𑌦𑌿𑌶𑍍𑌯 𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌤𑌃।  
𑌉𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌾𑌦𑌿 𑌯𑌤𑍍 𑌕𑌿𑌞𑍍𑌚𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌦𑌾𑌨𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯 𑌕𑌲𑍍𑌪𑌤𑍇॥  
—𑌸𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑌿𑌮𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌫𑌲𑌮𑍍  
𑌲𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌮𑍀𑌨𑌾𑌰𑌾𑌯𑌣𑌸𑌂𑌹𑌿𑌤𑌾/𑌖𑌣𑍍𑌡𑌃 ௧ (𑌕𑍃𑌤𑌯𑍁𑌗𑌸𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌨𑌃)/𑌅𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌃 ௨௬௮---  
𑌵𑍈𑌶𑌾𑌖𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌸𑌿𑌤𑍇 𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇 𑌤𑍃𑌤𑍀𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌪𑍁𑌨𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌸𑍌।  
𑌜𑌮𑌦𑌗𑍍𑌨𑌿𑌗𑍃𑌹𑍇 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌦𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌸𑍀𑌤𑍍𑌪𑌰𑌶𑍁𑌧𑍃𑌕𑍍 𑌹𑌰𑌿𑌃॥௨௨॥  
𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌰𑌾𑌜𑍇—  
𑌇𑌯𑌮𑍇𑌵 𑌤𑍃𑌤𑍀𑌯𑌾 𑌪𑌰𑌶𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌮𑌜𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍀॥ 𑌸𑌾 𑌚 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌦𑍋𑌷𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌪𑌿𑌨𑍀 𑌗𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌯𑌾।  
𑌤𑌦𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌂 𑌭𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌗𑌵𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌚𑌨𑌦𑍀𑌪𑌿𑌕𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑍍𑌕𑌨𑍍𑌦𑌭𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌯𑍋𑌃—  
𑌵𑍈𑌶𑌾𑌖𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌸𑌿𑌤𑍇 𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇 𑌤𑍃𑌤𑍀𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌪𑍁𑌨𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌸𑍌।  
𑌨𑌿𑌶𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌥𑌮𑍇 𑌯𑌾𑌮𑍇 𑌰𑌾𑌮𑌾𑌖𑍍𑌯𑌃 𑌸𑌮𑌯𑍇 𑌹𑌰𑌿𑌃।  
𑌸𑍍𑌵𑍋𑌚𑍍𑌚𑌗𑍈𑌃 𑌷𑌡𑍍𑌗𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌮𑌿𑌥𑍁𑌨𑍇 𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍁𑌸𑌂𑌸𑍍𑌥𑌿𑌤𑍇॥  
𑌰𑍇𑌣𑍁𑌕𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌯𑍋 𑌗𑌰𑍍𑌭𑌾𑌦𑌵𑌤𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌣𑍋 𑌵𑌿𑌭𑍁𑌃 𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌯𑌮𑍍।  
𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌯𑍇 𑌤𑌦𑍍𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌵𑌂𑌶𑌤𑌃 𑌸𑌮𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌤𑍌 𑌚 𑌪𑌰𑌾॥ 𑌅𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌥𑌾 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍈𑌵।

𑌮𑌾𑌘𑌶𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌥𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌤𑍁 𑌕𑍁𑌨𑍍𑌦𑌪𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌪𑍈𑌃 𑌸𑌦𑌾𑌶𑌿𑌵𑌮𑍍।  
𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌪𑍂𑌜𑍍𑌯 𑌯𑍋 𑌹𑌿 𑌨𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌽𑌽𑌶𑍀 𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌨𑍋𑌤𑌿 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌯𑌂 𑌨𑌰𑌃॥  
  
𑌸𑍁𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍁𑌵𑌾𑌚---  
𑌮𑌾𑌘𑍇 𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌿 𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌶𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑌾 𑌯𑌾 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌥𑍀 𑌮𑌹𑍀𑌪𑌤𑍇।  
𑌸𑌾 𑌶𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌾 𑌶𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌦𑌾 𑌨𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌶𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌂 𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍 𑌸𑌦𑍈𑌵 𑌹𑌿॥௬॥  
𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌦𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌕𑌂 𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌮 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌮𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌕𑍃𑌤𑌂 𑌵𑌿𑌭𑍋।  
𑌭𑌵𑍇𑌤𑍍𑌸𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌗𑍁𑌣𑌿𑌤𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌸𑌾𑌦𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌦𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌨𑌃॥௭॥  
𑌕𑍃𑌤𑍋𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑍋 𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌪𑍂𑌜𑌯𑍇𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌘𑍍𑌨𑌨𑌾𑌯𑌕𑌮𑍍।  
𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌹𑍋𑌮𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌕𑌂 𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌮 𑌭𑌵𑍇𑌤𑍍𑌸𑌾𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌕𑌂 𑌨𑍃𑌪॥௮॥  
𑌲𑌵𑌣𑌂 𑌚 𑌗𑍁𑌡𑌂 𑌶𑌾𑌕𑌂 𑌗𑍁𑌡𑌾𑌪𑍂𑌪𑌾𑌂𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌭𑌾𑌰𑌤।  
𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌤𑍁 𑌵𑌿𑌪𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌭𑍍𑌯𑌃 𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌸𑌾𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌕𑌂 𑌭𑌜𑍇𑌤𑍍॥௯॥  
𑌵𑌿𑌶𑍇𑌷𑌤𑌃 𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌯𑍋 𑌰𑌾𑌜𑌨𑍍 𑌪𑍂𑌜𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍋 𑌗𑍁𑌰𑍁𑌂 𑌨𑍃𑌪।  
𑌗𑍁𑌡𑌲𑌵𑌣𑌘𑍃𑌤𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍀𑌰 𑌸𑌦𑌾 𑌸𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌭𑌾𑌗𑍍𑌯𑌸𑌂𑌯𑍁𑌤𑌾𑌃॥௧௦॥  
(𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌭𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌯𑍇 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇 𑌶𑌤𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌧𑌸𑌾𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑌂𑌹𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌮𑍇 𑌪𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌣𑌿 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌥𑍀𑌕𑌲𑍍𑌪𑍇 𑌸𑍁𑌖𑌾𑌵𑌹𑌾𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌾𑌰𑌕𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌥𑍀𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌨𑌿𑌰𑍂𑌪𑌣𑌂 𑌨𑌾𑌮𑍈𑌕𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌂𑌶𑍋𑌽𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌤𑌃)

875685b084.d: Having entered the peak named Agastya after established Gaṅgādharagīṣpati in the ācārya Pīṭha and after subduing the Ugrabhairava through mantra, He stayed there itself. 𑌖𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌤𑌃 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌮𑍍 𑌉𑌦𑌾𑌰𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌵𑌿𑌭𑌵𑌃 𑌸𑌂𑌯𑌮𑍍𑌯 𑌸𑌚𑍍𑌚𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌘𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍍।  
𑌆𑌸𑍍𑌥𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌯𑌧𑌿𑌕𑌾𑌮𑌕𑍋𑌟𑌿 𑌸 𑌶𑌿𑌵𑌾𑌨𑍍 (௪௫) 𑌅𑌬𑍍𑌦𑌾𑌨𑍍 𑌅𑌗𑍇𑌽𑌗𑌾𑌲𑍍𑌲𑌯𑌂

—𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌶𑍍𑌲𑍋𑌕𑌮𑌞𑍍𑌜𑌰𑍀

876d1091f6.b: Observed on Rōhiṇī nakshatra of Mēṣaḥ (sidereal solar) month (Prātaḥ/paraviddha).
876d1091f6.d:
Between the 6th and 9th centuries, in South India, there existed 63 ardent devotees of Bhagavan Shiva, collectively known as the Nayanmars. These devout individuals, hailing from various walks of life including potters, fishermen, farmers, merchants, priests, hunters, and washermen, created devotional songs still sung by followers around the globe. Among these Nayanmars, Appar, Sambandar, and Sundarar, known for their Thevaram hymns, along with Manikkavasagar, are distinguished as the Samayacharyas or the ‘The Four’ (nālvar) revered teachers of the faith. They were instrumental in promoting the Shaiva Siddhanta philosophy and culture, effectively challenging the spread of Jainism and Buddhism. Their teachings centered around the concept that Shiva embodies love, and that embracing love for all beings and existence is essential in connecting with Shiva, the Supreme Being.

Mangaiyarkarasiyar, the 50th of the Nayanmars was the wife of another Nayanmar, Ninra Seer Nadumara Nayanmar, who was earlier known as Koon Pandyan, the hunchbacked Pandyan king of Madurai. Tiru Jnana Sambandar, a revered Nayanmar, arrived in Madurai and was invited into the city by Kulacchirai Nayanmar. Despite attempts by the Jains to harm Sambandar, his divine singing miraculously cured the king of his hunchback and alleviated his pain, leading to his return to Shaivism. Following his conversion, the king conquered northern kings at Tirunelveli, spreading Shaivism in those regions with the support of his wife. Both he and Mangayarkarasiyar deeply revered Sambandar and their dedication to their guru and Shaivism ultimately brought them divine grace.

876f0fd942.d:
The Phalguna Paurnami festival is a grand five-day celebration held annually at the Swami Pushkarini. Each day of the festival features a different set of deities taken for a celestial ride on a beautifully decorated float in the temple tank.

1. On the first day, Bhagavan Rama, along with Sita and Lakshmana, are worshipped and taken for a ride on the float.
2. The second day is dedicated to Bhagavan Krishna and Rukmini, who are also offered puja and taken on the float for a pleasure ride.

For the last three days, from Trayodashi to Paurnami:
1. Sri Malayappa Swami, accompanied by Sridevi and Bhudevi, are taken out for a ride in the temple tank.
2. The third day includes three rounds of the float, increasing to five rounds on the next day.
3. On the final day, the utsava murtis (festival deities) are taken for a splendid ride on the float for seven rounds, attracting a large number of pilgrims. The beauty of the deities is further enhanced by the charm of the full moon, making this day particularly special and visually stunning.

8798568060.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between śaniḥ and śukraḥ in uttaraprōṣṭhapadā mīnaḥ, center-to-center separation 0°54′42.76″.
8798568060.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°54′42.76″, 0°54′29.99″ apart, disc-to-disc. śaniḥ at uttaraprōṣṭhapadā-2 mīnaḥ (latitude 2°07′32.66″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude +0.97, elongation 14°48′02.40″ E). śukraḥ at uttaraprōṣṭhapadā-2 mīnaḥ (latitude 1°12′49.90″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -3.90, elongation 14°41′58.85″ E). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here śaniḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śaniḥ is taken as jayI over śukraḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

897c46f311.d: Observed on the day after dīpāvalī, on the , Govardhana Puja or annakūṭotsava involves constructing and worshipping a symbolic mountain of food to honour the Govardhana Hill and Bhagavan Krishna. The rituals include preparing a vast array of cooked dishes and dairy products, with the goal of achieving all worldly and spiritual success. On this day, cows are decorated, and worshipped as a form of Lakshmi Devi, with devotees praying for the removal of sins and the attainment of mōksha.

89812e731e.d: The Brahmotsavam of Nataraja at Chidambaram happens specially around the Aani Thirumanjana festival each year, for ten days. On this day, Nataraja gives darshan on a bhūta vahanam.

89982b0406.b: Partial lunar eclipse (parimāṇa ≈4.6 of 12 aṅgulas), Moon at the Rahu node (puccha/descending).
89982b0406.d: The eclipse is already in progress at moonrise (grastodaya). Umbral magnitude: 0.38 (parimāṇa ≈4.6 of the traditional 12 aṅgulas). Avoid food: 09:26►19:53 (from 3 yaamas before the yaama of first contact, until the eclipse's end). Those with janma nakshatra maghā/pūrvaphalgunī/uttaraphalgunī (preceding/grahaNa/succeeding), or pūrvāṣāḍhā (anujanma) or apabharaṇī (trijanma) get ashubha phala and should consider graha-shanti next day. By rashi: siṁhaḥ, kanyā, makaraḥ, vr̥ṣabhaḥ get more ashubha phala, dhanuḥ, kumbhaḥ, mēṣaḥ, karkaṭaḥ somewhat ashubha, tulā, vr̥śchikaḥ, mīnaḥ, mithunam shubha phala. General notes: Avoid touching anything other than what's needed for the anushthana (especially bed/mat/cloth) until the mokSha snAna after the eclipse ends -- this is grahaNa Ashaucham. Do not sleep or attend to natural impulses during the eclipse. Mantra japa and dAna during the puNya kAla are of immense benefit. Do not view the eclipse with naked eyes. Pregnant women should avoid exposure to the sun/moon's light during the respective eclipse.
89982b0406.r: - Food-restriction timing and graha-shanti nakshatra/rashi lists follow this pancAnga's "General notes for all grahanas" instructions.

89c1dd8845.d: On this day, From Wākharī, both the Dehu and Āl̤andī Pālkhīs—along with hundreds of others from across Maharashtra—walk the final stretch together to Panḍharpur. On this holy day of Ashadhi Ekadashi, the Wāri culminates. The pilgrims take a holy dip in the Chandrabhāgā river and complete the Pradakshina of the Vithoba temple, and of course, darshan of Bhagavan Viṭhobā, fulfilling their vow of the Wari.

89e59602ad.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between budhaḥ and śukraḥ in śravaṇaḥ makaraḥ, center-to-center separation 0°41′09.54″.
89e59602ad.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°41′09.54″, 0°41′02.18″ apart, disc-to-disc. budhaḥ at śravaṇaḥ-4 makaraḥ (latitude 2°00′24.36″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -1.28, elongation 5°47′39.66″ E). śukraḥ at śravaṇaḥ-4 makaraḥ (latitude 1°19′14.81″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -3.91, elongation 5°35′40.53″ E). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here budhaḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śukraḥ is taken as jayI over budhaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

8a1d6bbe59.d: Guruḥ sets into combustion (astamayaH), heading prāk (east), on 2025-Jun-10 20:30. At this moment guruḥ is at mr̥gaśīrṣam-4 mithunam (latitude 0°09′45.00″ S, moving r̥ju (direct)), magnitude -1.90, elongation 10°11′18.26″ E of the Sun. Combustion (mAudhyam) is generally considered to weaken a graha's ability to give full results in its significations; undertakings connected with guruḥ are traditionally best avoided until it re-emerges.

8a80989174.d: It is said in Vishnu Purāṇam that when Amavasya overlaps with one of nine nakshatras---Anuradha, Vishakha, Swati, Pushya, Ardra, Punarvasu, Shravishtha, Purvaproshthapada, or Shatabhishak---it is sacred even for Devas. For instance, Shraaddha done on an Amavasya joined with Anuradha, Vishakha, Swati keeps the pitrs satisfied for eight years. Likewise, on Pushya, Ardra and Punarvasu, the pitrs are satisfied for twelve years. It is said in the Smrtis, that if Amavasya falls on a Monday, Tuesday or Thursday, such a tithi is given the appellation puṣkalā and is as sacred as a solar eclipse. amāvāsyā of māgha month.
8a80989174.s:
𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇---

𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌧𑍇 𑌪𑌿𑌤𑍃𑌗𑌣𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍃𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌮𑌵𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌨𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌵𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌷𑌿𑌕𑍀𑌮𑍍॥  
𑌅𑌮𑌾𑌵𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌯𑌦𑌾 𑌪𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌯𑍇 𑌰𑍌𑌦𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌽𑌥𑌃 𑌪𑍁𑌨𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌸𑍌।  
𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌶𑌾𑌬𑍍𑌦𑌂 𑌤𑌦𑌾 𑌤𑍃𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌯𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌪𑌿𑌤𑌰𑍋𑌽𑌰𑍍𑌚𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌃॥  
𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌵𑌾𑌜𑍈𑌕𑌪𑌾𑌦𑍃𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇 𑌪𑌿𑌤𑍄𑌣𑌾𑌂 𑌤𑍃𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌮𑌿𑌚𑍍𑌛𑌤𑌾𑌮𑍍।  
𑌵𑌾𑌰𑍁𑌣𑍇 𑌚𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌯𑌮𑌾𑌵𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌮𑌪𑌿 𑌦𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌲𑌭𑌾।  
𑌨𑌵𑌸𑍍𑌵𑍃𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇𑌷𑍍𑌵𑌮𑌾𑌵𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌯𑌦𑍈𑌤𑍇𑌷𑍍𑌵𑌵𑌨𑍀𑌪𑌤𑍇॥  
𑌸𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌰𑍇---  
𑌅𑌮𑌾 𑌸𑍋𑌮𑍇𑌨 𑌭𑍌𑌮𑍇𑌨 𑌗𑍁𑌰𑍁𑌣𑌾 𑌵𑌾 𑌯𑍁𑌤𑌾 𑌯𑌦𑌿।  
𑌸𑌾 𑌤𑌿𑌥𑌿𑌃 𑌪𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌕𑌲𑌾 𑌨𑌾𑌮 𑌸𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌗𑍍𑌰𑌹𑌣𑌸𑌨𑍍𑌨𑌿𑌭𑌾॥

𑌅𑌯𑌨𑍇 𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍁𑌵𑍇 𑌚𑍈𑌵 𑌶𑌯𑌨𑍇 𑌬𑍋𑌧𑌨𑍇 𑌹𑌰𑍇𑌃।  
𑌅𑌨𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌵𑍍𑌯𑍋 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌷𑍁 𑌯𑍁𑌗𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌷𑍁॥

8b0261e88f.b: Observed on Paurṇamāsī tithi of every (lunar) month (Sūryōdayaḥ/paraviddha).

8b02d99b9f.b: Observed on Kr̥ṣṇa-Saptamī tithi of Māghaḥ (lunar) month (Madhyāhnaḥ/puurvaviddha).
8b02d99b9f.d: Nikṣubhā is the patnī of Surya Bhagavan. Worship Her along with arka (Surya) on nikṣubhārka-saptamī day.
8b02d99b9f.s:
𑌸𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌾 𑌤𑍁 𑌯𑌾 𑌨𑌾𑌰𑍀 𑌧𑍍𑌰𑍁𑌵𑌂 𑌸𑌾 𑌪𑍁𑌰𑍁𑌷𑍋 𑌭𑌵𑍇𑌤𑍍।  
𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍀 𑌚𑍈𑌵𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌮𑌂 𑌨𑌾𑌥𑌂 𑌯𑌤𑍍 𑌕𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌲𑌭𑌤𑍇 𑌶𑍃𑌣𑍁॥  
𑌨𑌿𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍁𑌭𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌕𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌂 𑌭𑌾𑌨𑍋𑌃 𑌸𑌦𑌾 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌤𑌿𑌵𑌿𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌧𑌨𑌮𑍍।  
𑌅𑌵𑌿𑌯𑍋𑌗𑌕𑌰𑌂 𑌵𑍀𑌰 𑌧𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌕𑌾𑌮𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌸𑌾𑌧𑌕𑌮𑍍॥  
𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑌥 𑌷𑌷𑍍𑌠𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌵𑌾 𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍌 𑌭𑌾𑌨𑌵𑍇 𑌦𑌿𑌨𑍇।  
𑌹𑌵𑌿𑌷𑌾 𑌹𑌵𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌹𑍋𑌮𑌂 𑌤𑍁 𑌸𑍋𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌃 𑌸𑌮𑌾𑌚𑌰𑍇𑌤𑍍॥  
𑌨𑌿𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍁𑌭𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌕𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌚𑍈𑌵𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌚𑌾𑌂 𑌕𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌮𑌯𑍀𑌂 𑌶𑍁𑌭𑌾𑌮𑍍।   
𑌰𑌾𑌜𑌤𑍀𑌂 𑌵𑌾𑌥 𑌵𑌾𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍀𑌂 𑌵𑌾 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌪𑌯𑍇𑌚𑍍𑌚 𑌘𑍃𑌤𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌭𑌿𑌃॥

8b429e32d6.s:
𑌸𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌰𑍇---  
𑌅𑌮𑌾 𑌪𑌾𑌤𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌵𑍈𑌧𑍃𑌤𑌿𑌰𑍇𑌵 𑌚।  
𑌅𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌚𑍈𑌵 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌗𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌲𑌯𑌃॥  
𑌚𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌸𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌯𑍋𑌪𑌰𑌾𑌗𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌗𑌜𑌚𑍍𑌛𑌾𑌯𑌾 𑌤𑌥𑍈𑌵 𑌚।  
𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌣𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌪𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌃 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌕𑌾𑌲𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌕𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌃॥  
𑌅𑌥𑌾𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑌾𑌃। 𑌤𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌃 𑌮𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌗𑌶𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌷𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌯𑌾𑌪𑌰𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌾𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌃 - 𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌚 𑌶𑍌𑌨𑌕𑌃---  
𑌹𑍇𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌶𑌿𑌶𑌿𑌰𑌯𑍋𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌾𑌮𑌪𑌰𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌾𑌣𑌾𑌮𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌮𑍀𑌷𑍍𑌵𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑌾𑌃 𑌇𑌤𑌿।  
𑌅𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌵𑌿𑌶𑍇𑌷𑌮𑌾𑌹 𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌃---  
𑌅𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌰𑍋𑌽𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌮𑍍𑌯𑍋𑌽𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍇𑌦𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑍌𑌷𑍍𑌠𑌪𑌦𑍇 𑌹𑍇𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌶𑌿𑌶𑌿𑌰𑌯𑍋𑌰𑌪𑌰𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇𑌷𑍁 𑌇𑌤𑌿। 𑌅𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌃 - 𑌨𑌵𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌃, 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍇𑌦𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌃 - 𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌃।  
𑌕𑌾𑌲𑌾𑌦𑌰𑍍𑌶𑍇𑌽𑌪𑌿---  
𑌮𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌗𑌶𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌷𑍇 𑌚 𑌪𑍌𑌷𑍇 𑌚 𑌮𑌾𑌘𑍇 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑍌𑌷𑍍𑌠𑍇 𑌚 𑌫𑌾𑌲𑍍𑌗𑍁𑌨𑍇।  
𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇𑌷𑍁 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍇𑌦𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌰𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌤𑌥𑌾𑌽𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌮𑍀।  
𑌇𑌤𑌿 𑌤𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌰𑍋𑌽𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌸𑍁 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌂 𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍀𑌤 𑌪𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌣𑌮𑍍।  
𑌆𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌲𑌾𑌯𑌨𑌃---  
𑌹𑍇𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌶𑌿𑌶𑌿𑌰𑌰𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑍋𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌾𑌮𑌪𑌿 𑌸𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌮𑍈𑌃।  
𑌸𑌮𑌰𑍍𑌥𑍈𑌰𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌕𑌾 𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌮𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌮𑍀𑌷𑍁 𑌚।   
𑌏𑌕𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌹𑌿 𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌶𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍇𑌨 𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌗𑍃𑌹𑍍𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌮𑌨𑌾 𑌇𑌤𑌿।  
𑌬𑍋𑌧𑌾𑌯𑌨𑍋𑌽𑌪𑌿---  
𑌉𑌪𑌰𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌾𑌨𑍍 𑌮𑌾𑌘𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑍌𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌮𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌅𑌪𑌰𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌨𑌵𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑌿𑌤𑌿 𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌯𑍇𑌤𑌾𑌪𑌿 𑌵𑌾𑌽𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑍇𑌵 𑌇𑌤𑌿।

8b7ee10246.b: Observed on Paurṇamāsī tithi of Vaiśākhaḥ (lunar) month (Sūryōdayaḥ/puurvaviddha).

8bb37cd155.b: Observed on Kr̥ṣṇa-Ṣaṣṭhī tithi of Śrāvaṇaḥ (lunar) month (Madhyāhnaḥ/paraviddha).
8bb37cd155.d: Hala Shashthi Vrata. THe plough is also worshipped by many. Women typically perform a vrata for the long life of their children.
8bb37cd155.s:
𑌨𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌯𑌸𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌧𑍁𑌃 ௨ 𑌪𑌰𑌿𑌚𑍍𑌛𑍇𑌦𑌃—  
𑌅𑌥 𑌭𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌪𑌦𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌷𑌷𑍍𑌠𑍀 𑌹𑌲𑌷𑌷𑍍𑌠𑍀। 𑌸𑌾 𑌚 𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌮𑍀𑌯𑍁𑌤𑌾 𑌗𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌯𑌾।  
𑌧𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌸𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌧𑍁𑌃 ௨ 𑌪𑌰𑌿𑌚𑍍𑌛𑍇𑌦𑌃—  
𑌭𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌪𑌦𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌷𑌷𑍍𑌠𑍀 𑌹𑌲𑌷𑌷𑍍𑌠𑍀 𑌲𑌲𑌹𑍀𑌛𑌠 𑌇𑌤𑌿 𑌖𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌤𑌾।  
𑌅𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌪𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌣𑌾𑌂 𑌦𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌘𑌾𑌯𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌰𑍋𑌗𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌂 𑌹𑌲𑌷𑌷𑍍𑌠𑍀𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌂 𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌭𑌿𑌃 𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌮𑍍।  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌨𑌾𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌃—  
𑌨𑌮𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌹𑌲𑌿𑌨𑌾𑌂 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌷𑍍𑌠 𑌨𑌮𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌮𑍁𑌸𑌲𑌾𑌯𑍁𑌧।  
𑌨𑌮𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌰𑍇𑌵𑌤𑍀𑌕𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤 𑌨𑌮𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌵𑌤𑍍𑌸𑌲॥  
𑌨𑌮𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌬𑌲𑌿𑌨𑌾𑌂 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌷𑍍𑌠 𑌨𑌮𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌧𑌰𑌣𑍀𑌧𑌰।  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌲𑌮𑍍𑌬𑌘𑍍𑌨 𑌨𑌮𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍇𑌽𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑌿 𑌮𑌾𑌂 𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌜॥

8bbf3c9b53.b: Observed on Śukla-Dvādaśī tithi of Vaiśākhaḥ (lunar) month (Sūryōdayaḥ/puurvaviddha).
8bbf3c9b53.s:
𑌵𑍈𑌶𑌾𑌖𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌿 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌪𑍂𑌜𑌯𑍇𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌧𑍁𑌸𑍂𑌦𑌨𑌮𑍍।  
𑌅𑌗𑍍𑌨𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌟𑍋𑌮𑌮𑌵𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌨𑍋𑌤𑌿 𑌸𑍋𑌮𑌲𑍋𑌕𑌂 𑌚 𑌗𑌚𑍍𑌛𑌤𑌿॥ (𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌭𑌾𑌰𑌤𑍇 𑌦𑌾𑌨𑌧𑌰𑍍𑌮𑍇)

8bc911a422.b: Observed on Bhānuḥ of Siṁhaḥ (sidereal solar) month (Sūryōdayaḥ/puurvaviddha).

8c3c6719e9.b: Observed on Kr̥ṣṇa-Dvādaśī tithi of Āśvayujaḥ (lunar) month (Sūryōdayaḥ/puurvaviddha).

8c40da5189.d: Special vrata day for Ganesha. In this month, Ganesha is worshipped as vighnarāja-mahāgaṇapatiḥ. Fast during the day and pray to Ganesha after moonrise, chanting the shloka mentioned. chaturthī tithi on a Sunday is specially sacred --- viśēṣaphalapradā.
8c40da5189.s:
𑌗𑌣𑌾𑌧𑌿𑌪𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌂 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑍇𑌶 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌥𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌪𑍂𑌜𑌿𑌤𑍋 𑌮𑌯𑌾।  
𑌕𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌂 𑌮𑍋𑌚𑌯𑍇𑌶𑌾𑌨 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌮𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌂 𑌚 𑌦𑍇𑌹𑌿 𑌮𑍇॥  
  
𑌯𑌦𑌾 𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌲𑍇𑌶𑌿𑌤𑍋 𑌮𑌰𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑍋 𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌦𑍁𑌃𑌖𑍈𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌦𑌾𑌰𑍁𑌣𑍈𑌃।  
𑌤𑌦𑌾 𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍇 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌥𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌵𑍈 𑌪𑍂𑌜𑌨𑍀𑌯𑍋 𑌗𑌣𑌾𑌧𑌿𑌪𑌃॥ (𑌭𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑌮𑍍)  
𑌨𑌾𑌰𑌦𑍀𑌯𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇 ௧௧௩.௬௦---  
𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌕𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌭𑌵𑍇𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌿 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌥𑍀 𑌰𑌵𑌿𑌵𑌾𑌰𑌯𑍁𑌕𑍍।  
𑌸𑌾𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌾𑌰𑌕𑌾 𑌵𑌾 𑌵𑌿𑌪𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰 𑌸𑌾 𑌵𑌿𑌶𑍇𑌷𑌫𑌲𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌦𑌾॥

8cc1588acf.b: Observed on Śukla-Caturthī tithi falling on Maṅgalaḥ (Dinamaana/puurvaviddha).
8cc1588acf.d: Chaturthī tithi on a Tuesday is as sacred as a solar eclipse. When it occurs in śuklapakṣa, it is called sukhā. Good day for doing puja of Ganesha/Subrahmanya with naivedyam of modakam/millet flour respectively.
8cc1588acf.s:
𑌸𑍁𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍁𑌵𑌾𑌚---  
𑌸𑍁𑌖𑌾𑌵𑌹𑌾 𑌚 𑌸𑍁𑌸𑍁𑌖𑌾 𑌸𑍌𑌭𑌾𑌗𑍍𑌯𑌕𑌰𑌣𑍀 𑌪𑌰𑌮𑍍॥௧௧॥  
𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌥𑍀 𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍁𑌶𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌦𑍂𑌲 𑌰𑍂𑌪𑌸𑍌𑌭𑌾𑌗𑍍𑌯𑌦𑌾 𑌶𑍁𑌭𑌾।  
𑌸𑍁𑌖𑌾𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌂 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌰𑍂𑌪𑌦𑌂 𑌭𑌾𑌗𑍍𑌯𑌦𑌂 𑌤𑌥𑌾॥௧௨॥  
𑌸𑍁𑌸𑍂𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌮𑌂 𑌸𑍁𑌕𑌰𑌂 𑌧𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌮𑌿𑌹 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌸𑍁𑌖𑌾𑌵𑌹𑌮𑍍।  
𑌪𑌰𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌫𑌲𑌦𑌂 𑌵𑍀𑌰 𑌦𑌿𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌰𑍂𑌪𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌦𑌾𑌯𑌕𑌮𑍍॥௧௩॥  
𑌹𑌸𑌿𑌤𑌂 𑌲𑌲𑌿𑌤𑌂 𑌚𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌂 𑌚𑍇𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌿𑌤𑌂 𑌚 𑌸𑍁𑌖𑌾𑌵𑌹𑌮𑍍।  
𑌸𑌵𑌿𑌲𑌾𑌸𑌭𑍁𑌜𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇𑌪𑌂 𑌚𑌙𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌮𑌂 𑌚𑍇𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌿𑌤𑌂 𑌶𑍁𑌭𑌮𑍍॥௧௪॥  
𑌸𑍁𑌖𑌾𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑍇𑌨 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍇𑌷𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑍁𑌖𑌂 𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍁𑌕𑍁𑌲𑍋𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌹।  
𑌕𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌯𑍇𑌨 𑌪𑍂𑌜𑌿𑌤𑍇 𑌚𑍇𑌶𑍇 𑌵𑌿𑌘𑍍𑌨𑍇𑌶𑍇 𑌶𑌿𑌵𑌯𑍋𑌃 𑌸𑍁𑌤𑍇॥௧௫॥  
𑌯𑌦𑌾 𑌶𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌥𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌤𑍁 𑌵𑌾𑌰𑍋 𑌭𑍌𑌮𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌵𑍈 𑌭𑌵𑍇𑌤𑍍।  
𑌤𑌦𑌾 𑌸𑌾 𑌸𑍁𑌖𑌦𑌾 𑌜𑍍𑌞𑍇𑌯𑌾 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌥𑍀 𑌵𑍈 𑌸𑍁𑌖𑍇𑌤𑌿 𑌚॥௧௬॥  
𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾 𑌮𑍈𑌥𑍁𑌨𑌮𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌯 𑌸𑍍𑌥𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌭𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌤𑍁 𑌹𑌿𑌮𑌾𑌚𑌲𑍇।  
𑌭𑍀𑌮𑍋𑌮𑌾𑌭𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌬𑌾𑌹𑍋 𑌰𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌬𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍁𑌶𑍍𑌚𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌤𑌃 𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌿𑌤𑍌॥௧௭॥  
𑌮𑍇𑌦𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌸 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌨𑍇𑌨 𑌸𑍁𑌖𑍇𑌨 𑌵𑌿𑌧𑍃𑌤𑍋𑌽𑌨𑌯𑌾।  
𑌜𑌾𑌤𑍋𑌽𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌃 𑌸 𑌕𑍁𑌜𑍋 𑌵𑍀𑌰 𑌰𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍋 𑌰𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌸𑌮𑍁𑌦𑍍𑌭𑌵𑌃॥௧௮॥  
𑌮𑌮𑌾𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌤𑍋 𑌯𑌥𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌪𑌨𑍍𑌨𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌦𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌾𑌰𑌕𑍋 𑌹𑍍𑌯𑌯𑌮𑍍।  
𑌅𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌦𑍋𑌽𑌙𑍍𑌗𑍋𑌪𑌕𑌾𑌰𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌅𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌂 𑌤𑍁 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌦𑍋 𑌨𑍃𑌣𑌾𑌮𑍍॥௧௯॥  
𑌸𑍌𑌭𑌾𑌗𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌕𑌰𑍋 𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌦𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌾𑌰𑌕𑍋 𑌮𑌤𑌃।  
𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌥𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌨𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍇𑌨 𑌯𑍋 𑌵𑍈 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌾𑌸𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌤𑌃॥௨௦॥  
𑌉𑌪𑍋𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌤𑌿 𑌨𑌰𑍋 𑌰𑌾𑌜𑌨𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌰𑍀 𑌵𑌾 𑌨𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌮𑌾𑌨𑌸𑌾।  
𑌪𑍂𑌜𑌯𑍇𑌚𑍍𑌚 𑌕𑍁𑌜𑌂 𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌰𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌪𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌪𑌵𑌿𑌲𑍇𑌪𑌨𑍈𑌃॥௨௧॥  
𑌗𑌣𑍇𑌶𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌥𑌮𑌂 𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌯𑍋𑌽𑌰𑍍𑌚𑌯𑍇𑌚𑍍𑌛𑍍𑌰𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌯𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌤𑌃।  
𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌤𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌯𑌚𑍍𑌛𑍇𑌤𑍍𑌸 𑌸𑍌𑌭𑌾𑌗𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌰𑍂𑌪𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌪𑌦𑌮𑍍॥௨௨॥  
𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌂 𑌚 𑌕𑍃𑌤𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌕𑌲𑍍𑌪𑌃 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌕𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌯𑌥𑌾𑌵𑌿𑌧𑌿।  
𑌗𑍃𑌹𑍀𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌮𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌕𑌾𑌂 𑌵𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍇𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌣𑌾𑌨𑍇𑌨 𑌭𑌾𑌰𑌤॥௨௩॥  
𑌇𑌹 𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌂 𑌵𑌨𑍍𑌦𑌿𑌤𑌾 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌂 𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍇𑌨𑍋𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌰𑌤𑌾 𑌕𑌿𑌲।  
𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌮𑍇 𑌦𑌹 𑌪𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌯𑌾 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌸𑌞𑍍𑌚𑌿𑌤𑌮𑍍॥௨௪॥  
𑌇𑌮𑌂 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌂 𑌪𑌠𑌨𑍍𑌵𑍀𑌰 𑌆𑌦𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌦𑌰𑍍𑌶𑌯𑍇𑌤𑍍।  
𑌆𑌦𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌰𑌶𑍍𑌮𑌿𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌪𑍂𑌤𑌾𑌂 𑌗𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌾𑌜𑌲𑌕𑌣𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌮𑍍॥௨௫॥  
𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌮𑍃𑌦𑌂 𑌶𑌿𑌰𑌸𑌿 𑌤𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌙𑍍𑌗𑍇𑌷𑍁 𑌚 𑌯𑍋𑌜𑌯𑍇𑌤𑍍।  
𑌤𑌤𑌃 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍀𑌤 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍇𑌤 𑌜𑌲𑌂 𑌪𑍁𑌨𑌃॥௨௬॥  
𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌮𑌾𑌪𑍋 𑌯𑍋𑌨𑌿𑌃 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍇𑌷𑌾𑌂 𑌦𑍈𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌦𑌾𑌨𑌵𑌦𑍍𑌯𑍌𑌕𑌸𑌾𑌮𑍍।  
𑌸𑍍𑌵𑍇𑌦𑌾𑌣𑍍𑌡𑌜𑍋𑌦𑍍𑌭𑌿𑌦𑌾𑌂 𑌚𑍈𑌵 𑌰𑌸𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌂 𑌪𑌤𑌯𑍇 𑌨𑌮𑌃॥௨௭॥  
𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍋𑌽𑌹𑌂 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌤𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌥𑍇𑌷𑍁 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌵𑌣𑍇𑌷𑍁 𑌚।  
𑌤𑌡𑌾𑌗𑍇𑌷𑍁 𑌚 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍇𑌷𑍁 𑌮𑌾𑌨𑌸𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌸𑌰𑌃𑌸𑍁 𑌚॥௨௮॥  
𑌨𑌦𑍀𑌷𑍁 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌖𑌾𑌤𑍇𑌷𑍁 𑌸𑍁𑌤𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌥𑍇𑌷𑍁 𑌹𑍍𑌰𑌦𑍇𑌷𑍁 𑌵𑍈।  
𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌨𑍍 𑌪𑌠𑌨𑍍𑌨𑌿𑌮𑌂 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌂 𑌤𑌤𑌃 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌸𑌮𑌾𑌚𑌰𑍇𑌤𑍍॥௨௯॥  
𑌤𑌤𑌃 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌶𑍁𑌚𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌭𑍂𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌗𑍃𑌹𑌮𑌾𑌗𑌤𑍍𑌯 𑌵𑍈 𑌸𑍍𑌪𑍃𑌶𑍇𑌤𑍍।  
𑌦𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌤𑍍𑌥𑍌 𑌶𑌮𑍀𑌂 𑌸𑍍𑌪𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌟𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌗𑌾𑌂 𑌚 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌣 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌵𑌿𑌤𑍍॥௩௦॥  
𑌦𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌨𑌮𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌣 𑌶𑍁𑌚𑍌 𑌭𑍂𑌮𑍌 𑌸𑌮𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌥𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌮𑍍।  
𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌂 𑌦𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍇𑌽𑌮𑍃𑌤𑌨𑌾𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌿 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌦𑍇𑌵𑍈𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌵𑌨𑍍𑌦𑌿𑌤𑌾॥௩௧॥  
𑌵𑌨𑍍𑌦𑌿𑌤𑌾 𑌦𑌹 𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌂 𑌦𑍁𑌰𑌿𑌤𑌂 𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌯𑌾 𑌕𑍃𑌤𑌮𑍍॥௩௨॥  
𑌶𑌮𑍀𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌵𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑌿 𑌤𑌨𑍍𑌨𑌿𑌬𑍋𑌧 𑌮𑌹𑍀𑌪𑌤𑍇।  
𑌪𑌵𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌣𑌾𑌂 𑌪𑌵𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌂 𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌂 𑌕𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌪𑍀 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌥𑌿𑌤𑌾 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍁𑌤𑍌।  
𑌶𑌮𑍀 𑌶𑌮𑌯 𑌮𑍇 𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌂 𑌨𑍂𑌨𑌂 𑌵𑍇𑌤𑍍𑌸𑌿 𑌧𑌰𑌾𑌧𑌰𑌾𑌨𑍍॥௩௩॥  
𑌅𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌤𑍍𑌥𑌾𑌲𑌮𑍍𑌭𑌨𑍇 𑌵𑍀𑌰 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌮𑍇𑌤𑌂 𑌨𑌿𑌬𑍋𑌧 𑌮𑍇।  
𑌨𑍇𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌸𑍍𑌪𑌨𑍍𑌦𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌜𑌂 𑌦𑍁𑌃𑌖𑌂 𑌦𑍁𑌃𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌪𑍍𑌨𑌂 𑌦𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌚𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌨𑌮𑍍।  
𑌶𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌂 𑌚 𑌸𑌮𑍁𑌦𑍍𑌯𑍋𑌗𑌮𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌤𑍍𑌥 𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌂 𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌮𑌸𑍍𑌵 𑌮𑍇॥௩௪॥  
𑌇𑌮𑌂 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌂 𑌪𑌠𑌨𑍍𑌵𑍀𑌰 𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌵𑍈 𑌸𑍍𑌪𑌰𑍍𑌶𑌨𑌂 𑌬𑍁𑌧𑌃।  
𑌤𑌤𑍋 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑍍𑌯𑍈 𑌤𑍁 𑌗𑌾𑌂 𑌦𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌵𑍀𑌰𑌂 𑌕𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌦𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌿𑌣𑌾𑌮𑍍।  
𑌸𑌮𑌾𑌲𑌭𑍍𑌯 𑌤𑍁 𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍇𑌨 𑌤𑌤𑍋 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌮𑍁𑌦𑍀𑌰𑌯𑍇𑌤𑍍॥௩௫॥  
𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌮𑌯𑍀 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌿 𑌮𑍁𑌨𑌿𑌭𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌸𑍁𑌪𑍂𑌜𑌿𑌤𑌾।  
𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌸𑍍𑌪𑍃𑌶𑌾𑌮𑌿 𑌵𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍇 𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌂 𑌵𑌨𑍍𑌦𑌿𑌤𑌾 𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌹𑌾 𑌭𑌵॥௩௬॥  
𑌇𑌮𑌂 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌂 𑌪𑌠𑌨𑍍𑌵𑍀𑌰 𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌾𑌸𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌤𑌃।  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌦𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌿𑌣𑌂 𑌤𑍁 𑌯𑌃 𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑌰𑍍𑌜𑍁𑌨𑌂 𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍁𑌨𑌨𑍍𑌦𑌨।  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌦𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌿𑌣𑍀𑌕𑍃𑌤𑌾 𑌤𑍇𑌨 𑌪𑍃𑌥𑌿𑌵𑍀 𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌨 𑌸𑌂𑌶𑌯𑌃॥௩௭॥  
𑌏𑌵𑌂 𑌮𑍌𑌨𑍇𑌨 𑌚𑌾𑌽𑌽𑌗𑌤𑍍𑌯 𑌤𑌤𑍋 𑌵𑌹𑍍𑌨𑌿𑌗𑍃𑌹𑌂 𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌜𑍇𑌤𑍍।  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌾𑌲𑍍𑌯 𑌚 𑌮𑍃𑌦𑌾 𑌪𑌾𑌦𑌾𑌵𑌾𑌚𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍋𑌗𑍍𑌨𑌿𑌗𑍃𑌹𑌂 𑌵𑌿𑌶𑍇𑌤𑍍।  
𑌹𑍋𑌮𑌂 𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍀𑌤 𑌏𑌭𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌪𑌦𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌰𑍈𑌃॥௩௮॥  
𑌶𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌯 𑌶𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌪𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌯 𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍋𑌣𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌭𑌵𑌾𑌯 𑌚।  
𑌕𑍁𑌜𑌾𑌯 𑌲𑌲𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌾𑌯 𑌲𑍋𑌹𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌾𑌯 𑌵𑍈 𑌤𑌥𑌾॥௩௯॥  
𑍐𑌕𑌾𑌰𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌕𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍈𑌃 𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌹𑌾𑌕𑌾𑌰𑌸𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌤𑍈𑌃।  
𑌅𑌷𑍍𑌟𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌰𑌶𑌤𑌂 𑌵𑍀𑌰 𑌅𑌰𑍍𑌧𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌧𑌮𑌰𑍍𑌧𑌮𑍇𑌵 𑌚॥௪௦॥  
𑌏𑌤𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌪𑌦𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌶𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌵𑌾 𑌕𑌾𑌮𑌤𑍋 𑌨𑍃𑌪।  
𑌖𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌰𑍈𑌃 𑌸𑍁𑌸𑌮𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌭𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌚𑌾𑌽𑌽𑌜𑍍𑌯𑌦𑍁𑌗𑍍𑌧𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌵𑍈𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌲𑍈𑌃॥௪௧॥  
𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌯𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌵𑌿𑌧𑍈𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌯𑍈𑌃 𑌶𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌸𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌤𑌃।  
𑌹𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌽𑌽𑌹𑍁𑌤𑍀𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌤𑍋 𑌵𑍀𑌰 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌂 𑌸𑌂𑌸𑍍𑌥𑌾𑌪𑌯𑍇𑌤𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌿𑌤𑍌॥௪௨॥  
𑌸𑍌𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌂 𑌰𑌾𑌜𑌤𑌂 𑌵𑌾𑌽𑌪𑌿 𑌶𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌦𑌾𑌰𑍁𑌮𑌯𑌂 𑌨𑍃𑌪।  
𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌦𑌾𑌰𑍁𑌮𑌯𑌂 𑌵𑌾𑌽𑌪𑌿 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌖𑌣𑍍𑌡𑌚𑌨𑍍𑌦𑌨𑍈𑌰𑌪𑌿॥௪௩॥  
𑌤𑌾𑌮𑍍𑌰𑍇 𑌪𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍇 𑌰𑍌𑌪𑍍𑌯𑌮𑌯𑍇 𑌚𑌾𑌽𑌽𑌜𑍍𑌯𑌕𑍁𑌙𑍍𑌕𑍁𑌮𑌕𑍇𑌸𑌰𑍈𑌃।  
𑌅𑌨𑍍𑌯𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌲𑍋𑌹𑌿𑌤𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌽𑌪𑌿 𑌪𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌪𑍈𑌃 𑌪𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍈𑌃 𑌫𑌲𑍈𑌰𑌪𑌿।  
𑌰𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍈𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌵𑌿𑌵𑌿𑌧𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍀𑌰 𑌅𑌥 𑌵𑌾 𑌶𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌤𑍋𑌽𑌰𑍍𑌚𑌯𑍇𑌤𑍍॥௪௪॥  
𑌯𑌾𑌵𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌸𑍃𑌜𑌤𑍇 𑌵𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌂 𑌵𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌵𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌵𑍀𑌰 𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌤𑌃।  
𑌤𑌾𑌵𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌧𑌤𑍇 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌦𑌾𑌤𑍁𑌂 𑌶𑌤𑌸𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌕𑌮𑍍॥௪௫॥  
𑌅𑌨𑍍𑌯𑍇 𑌤𑌾𑌮𑍍𑌰𑌮𑌯𑍇 𑌪𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍇 𑌵𑌂𑌶𑌜𑍇 𑌮𑍃𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌯𑍇𑌽𑌪𑌿 𑌵𑌾।  
𑌪𑍂𑌜𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌨𑌰𑌾𑌃 𑌶𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌕𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌕𑍁𑌙𑍍𑌕𑍁𑌮𑌕𑍇𑌸𑌰𑍈𑌃।  
𑌪𑍁𑌰𑍁𑌷𑌾𑌕𑍃𑌤𑌿𑌕𑍃𑌤𑌂 𑌪𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌇𑌮𑌂 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍈𑌃 𑌸𑌮𑌰𑍍𑌚𑌯𑍇𑌤𑍍॥௪௬॥  
𑌅𑌗𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌮𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌧𑍇𑌤𑌿 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌣 𑌗𑌨𑍍𑌧𑌪𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌪𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌭𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌥𑌾।  
𑌧𑍂𑌪𑍈𑌰𑌭𑍍𑌯𑌰𑍍𑌚𑍍𑌯 𑌵𑌿𑌧𑌿𑌵𑌦𑍍𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌣𑌾𑌯 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌦𑍀𑌯𑌤𑍇॥௪௭॥  
𑌗𑍁𑌡𑍌𑌦𑌨𑌂 𑌘𑍃𑌤𑌂 𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍀𑌰𑌂 𑌗𑍋𑌧𑍂𑌮𑌾𑌞𑍍𑌛𑌾𑌲𑌿𑌤𑌣𑍍𑌡𑍁𑌲𑌾𑌨𑍍।  
𑌅𑌵𑍇𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌯 𑌶𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌂 𑌦𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌵𑍈 𑌦𑌰𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌰𑍋 𑌵𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌵𑌾𑌂𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌥𑌾॥௪௮॥  
𑌵𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌶𑌾𑌠𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌨 𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌵𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌮𑌾𑌨𑍇 𑌧𑌨𑍇 𑌨𑍃𑌪।  
𑌵𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌶𑌾𑌠𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌹𑌿 𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌣𑍋 𑌨𑌾𑌮𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌫𑌲𑌭𑌾𑌗𑍍𑌭𑌵𑍇𑌤𑍍॥௪௯॥  
𑌶𑌤𑌾𑌨𑍀𑌕 𑌉𑌵𑌾𑌚  
𑌅𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌾𑌰𑌕𑍇𑌣 𑌸𑌂𑌯𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌾 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌥𑍀 𑌨𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌭𑍋𑌜𑌨𑍈𑌃।  
𑌉𑌪𑍋𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌕𑌤𑌿𑌮𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾 𑌤𑍁 𑌉𑌤𑌾𑌹𑍋 𑌸𑌕𑍃𑌦𑍇𑌵 𑌤𑍁॥௫௦॥  
𑌸𑍁𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍁𑌵𑌾𑌚  
𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌥𑍀 𑌸𑌾 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌥𑍀 𑌸𑌾 𑌯𑌦𑌾𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌾𑌰𑌕𑌸𑌂𑌯𑍁𑌤𑌾।  
𑌉𑌪𑍋𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍈𑌵 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌦𑍇𑌯𑍋 𑌵𑌿𑌧𑌿𑌵𑌦𑍍𑌗𑍁𑌡𑌃॥௫௧॥  
𑌉𑌪𑍋𑌷𑍍𑌯 𑌨𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍇𑌨 𑌵𑌿𑌭𑍋 𑌚𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌃 𑌕𑍁𑌜𑌸𑌂𑌯𑍁𑌤𑌾।  
𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌥𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌚 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌥𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌚 𑌵𑌿𑌧𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌶𑍃𑌣𑍁 𑌯𑌾𑌦𑍃𑌶𑌮𑍍॥௫௨॥  
𑌸𑍌𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌂 𑌤𑍁 𑌕𑍁𑌜𑌂 𑌕𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌸𑌵𑌿𑌨𑌾𑌯𑌕𑌮𑌾𑌦𑌰𑌾𑌤𑍍।  
𑌦𑌶𑌸𑍌𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌿𑌕𑌂 𑌮𑍁𑌖𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌦𑌶𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌧𑌮𑌰𑍍𑌧𑌮𑍇𑌵 𑌚॥௫௩॥  
𑌸𑍌𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌣𑌪𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍇 𑌰𑍌𑌪𑍍𑌯𑍇 𑌵𑌾 𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌤𑌾𑌮𑍍𑌰𑌮𑌯𑍇𑌽𑌪𑌿 𑌵𑌾।  
𑌵𑌿𑌂𑌶𑌤𑍍𑌪𑌲𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌪𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌣𑌿 𑌵𑌿𑌂𑌶𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌰𑍍𑌧𑌪𑌲𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌵𑌾॥௫௪॥  
𑌵𑌿𑌂𑌶𑌤𑍍𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌷𑌾𑌣𑌿 𑌵𑌾 𑌵𑍀𑌰 𑌵𑌿𑌂𑌶𑌦𑌰𑍍𑌧𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌧𑌮𑍇𑌵 𑌵𑌾।  
𑌰𑍌𑌪𑍍𑌯𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌖𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌪𑌲𑌂 𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌪𑌲𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌧𑌮𑌰𑍍𑌧𑌮𑍇𑌵 𑌚॥௫௫॥  
𑌶𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌵𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍈𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌚 𑌪𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍇 𑌤𑌾𑌮𑍍𑌰𑌮𑌯𑍇𑌽𑌪𑌿 𑌤𑍁।  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌠𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌯 𑌗𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍇𑌶𑌂 𑌵𑍈 𑌵𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍈𑌃 𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌪𑌰𑌿𑌵𑍇𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌿𑌤𑌮𑍍।  
𑌵𑌿𑌵𑌿𑌧𑍈𑌃 𑌸𑌾𑌧𑌕𑍈 𑌰𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍈𑌃 𑌪𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌪𑍈 𑌰𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍈𑌃 𑌸𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌤𑌮𑍍॥௫௬॥  
𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌣𑌾𑌯 𑌸𑌦𑌾 𑌦𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌦𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌿𑌣𑌾𑌸𑌹𑌿𑌤𑌂 𑌨𑍃𑌪।  
𑌵𑌾𑌚𑌕𑌾𑌯 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌬𑌾𑌹𑍋 𑌗𑍁𑌣𑌿𑌨𑍇 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌯𑌸𑍇 𑌨𑍃𑌪॥௫௭॥  
𑌇𑌤𑌿 𑌤𑍇 𑌕𑌥𑌿𑌤𑌾 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌤𑌿𑌥𑍀𑌨𑌾𑌮𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌮𑌾 𑌤𑌿𑌥𑌿𑌃।  
𑌯𑌾𑌮𑍁𑌪𑍋𑌷𑍍𑌯 𑌨𑌰𑍋 𑌰𑍂𑌪𑌂 𑌦𑌿𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌮𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌨𑍋𑌤𑌿 𑌭𑌾𑌰𑌤॥௫௮॥  
𑌕𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌽𑌽𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌯𑌸𑌮𑌂 𑌵𑍀𑌰𑌂 𑌤𑍇𑌜𑌸𑌾 𑌰𑌵𑌿𑌸𑌨𑍍𑌨𑌿𑌭𑌮𑍍।  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌭𑌯𑌾 𑌰𑌵𑌿𑌕𑌲𑍍𑌪𑌂 𑌚 𑌸𑌮𑍀𑌰𑌬𑌲𑌸𑌂𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌤𑌮𑍍॥௫௯॥  
𑌈𑌦𑍃𑌗𑍍𑌰𑍂𑌪𑌂 𑌸𑌮𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌯𑍇𑌹 𑌯𑌾𑌤𑌿 𑌭𑍌𑌮𑌸𑌦𑍋 𑌨𑍃𑌪।  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌸𑌾𑌦𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌘𑍍𑌨𑌨𑌾𑌥𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌗𑌣𑌪𑌤𑍇𑌰𑍍𑌨𑍃𑌪॥௬௦॥  
𑌪𑌠𑌤𑌾𑌂 𑌶𑍃𑌣𑍍𑌵𑌤𑌾𑌂 𑌰𑌾𑌜𑌨𑍍𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌤𑌾𑌂 𑌚 𑌵𑌿𑌶𑍇𑌷𑌤𑌃।  
𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌹𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍀𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌸𑌂𑌶𑌯𑌃।  
𑌋𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌿𑌂 𑌵𑍃𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌿𑌂 𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌲𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌮𑍀𑌂 𑌲𑌭𑌤𑍇 𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌸𑌂𑌶𑌯𑌃॥௬௧॥  
---𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌭𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌯𑍇 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇 𑌶𑌤𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌧𑌸𑌾𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑌂𑌹𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌮𑍇 𑌪𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌣𑌿 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌥𑍀𑌕𑌲𑍍𑌪𑍇 𑌸𑍁𑌖𑌾𑌵𑌹𑌾𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌾𑌰𑌕𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌥𑍀𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌨𑌿𑌰𑍂𑌪𑌣𑌂 𑌨𑌾𑌮𑍈𑌕𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌂𑌶𑍋𑌽𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌤𑌃

8d4e35aad0.d: Dvadashi tithi, which starts after sunrise on a day and ends before sunrise on the next. O brāhmaṇa, merely hearing the account of Trispṛśā, which is both wonderful and thrilling, grants the religious merit equivalent to bathing in the Gaṅgā. Fasting on Trispṛśā yields the same rewards as performing thousands of Aśvamedha sacrifices and hundreds of Vājapeya sacrifices. It brings liberation not only to oneself but also to one's paternal, maternal, and personal family lines, and one is honoured in the world of Viṣṇu. The merit obtained from fasting on Trispṛśā is equal to that of visiting millions of holy and sacred places. O noble brāhmaṇa, all those—whether they are brāhmaṇas, evil-minded kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, śūdras, or persons of other jātis—achieve salvation after leaving the earth. This vow is the king of all vows, much like how the revered dvādaśākṣarī is, among mantras. It is the foremost of vows for those who observe it. It was first followed by Brahmā and then by royal sages. What more can be said? Trispṛśā bestows (even) salvation.
8d4e35aad0.s:
𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌦𑍇𑌵 𑌉𑌵𑌾𑌚---  
𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌜𑍈𑌤𑌤𑍍 𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌪𑍃𑌶𑌾𑌖𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌨𑌮𑌦𑍍𑌭𑍁𑌤𑌂 𑌰𑍋𑌮𑌹𑌰𑍍𑌷𑌣𑌮𑍍।  
𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌤𑍁 𑌲𑌭𑌤𑍇 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌗𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌾𑌤𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌲𑌭𑍇𑌤𑍍॥௭௮॥  
𑌅𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌮𑍇𑌧𑌸𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌣𑌿 𑌵𑌾𑌜𑌪𑍇𑌯𑌶𑌤𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌚।  
𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌸𑌮𑌵𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌨𑍋𑌤𑌿 𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌪𑍃𑌶𑌾𑌸𑌮𑍁𑌪𑍋𑌷𑌣𑌾𑌤𑍍॥௭௯॥  
𑌪𑌿𑌤𑍃𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍋 𑌮𑌾𑌤𑍃𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌚𑍈𑌵𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌮𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌕𑌃।  
𑌤𑍈𑌃 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍈𑌃 𑌸𑌹 𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌭𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍋 𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌲𑍋𑌕𑍇 𑌮𑌹𑍀𑌯𑌤𑍇॥௮௦॥  
𑌤𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌕𑍋𑌟𑌿𑌷𑍁 𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌕𑍋𑌟𑌿𑌷𑍁 𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌫𑌲𑌮𑍍।  
𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌫𑌲𑌂 𑌸𑌮𑌵𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌨𑍋𑌤𑌿 𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌪𑍃𑌶𑌾𑌸𑌮𑍁𑌪𑍋𑌷𑌣𑌾𑌤𑍍॥௮௧॥  
𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌣𑌾 𑌯𑍇𑌽𑌪𑌿 𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌯𑌾𑌃 𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌮𑌾𑌨𑌸𑌾𑌃।  
𑌵𑍈𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌵𑌾 𑌶𑍂𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌜𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌨𑍋 𑌯𑍇 𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌚𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌜𑌾𑌤𑌯𑌃॥௮௨॥  
𑌤𑍇 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍇 𑌮𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌮𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌭𑍁𑌵𑌂 𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌜𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌮।  
𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌣𑌾𑌂 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌰𑌾𑌜𑍋𑌽𑌥 𑌯𑌥𑌾 𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑍍 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌶𑌾𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌰𑌃॥௮௩॥  
𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌂 𑌚 𑌯𑌥𑌾 𑌚𑍈𑌷𑌾 𑌯𑍇𑌨 𑌵𑍈 𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌪𑍃𑌶𑌾 𑌕𑍃𑌤𑌾।  
𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌣𑌾 𑌚 𑌕𑍃𑌤𑌾 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌂 𑌪𑌶𑍍𑌚𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌜𑌰𑍍𑌷𑌿𑌭𑌿𑌃 𑌕𑍃𑌤𑌾॥௮௪॥  
𑌅𑌨𑍍𑌯𑍇𑌷𑌾𑌂 𑌕𑌾 𑌕𑌥𑌾 𑌵𑌤𑍍𑌸 𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌪𑍃𑌶𑌾 𑌮𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌦𑌾𑌯𑌿𑌨𑍀।  
---𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌪𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌮𑍇 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣 𑌉𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌰𑌖𑌣𑍍𑌡 𑌉𑌮𑌾𑌪𑌤𑌿𑌨𑌾𑌰𑌦𑌸𑌂𑌵𑌾𑌦𑍇 𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌪𑍃𑌶𑌾𑌖𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌨𑌾𑌮 𑌪𑌞𑍍𑌚𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌂𑌶𑍋𑌽𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌃॥௩௫॥  
𑌕𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌸𑌾𑌰𑌸𑌮𑍁𑌚𑍍𑌚𑌯𑍇 𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌕𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌕𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌯𑍇 𑌸𑍍𑌮𑍃𑌤𑌿-𑌵𑌚𑌨𑌮𑍍---  
𑌏𑌕𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍀 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍀 𑌚 𑌰𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌶𑍇𑌷𑍇 𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑍋𑌦𑌶𑍀।  
𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌪𑍃𑌶𑌮𑌹𑍋𑌰𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌂 𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌸𑌾𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌕𑌂 𑌫𑌲𑌮𑍍॥ 𑌇𑌤𑌿। 𑌸𑌾𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌕𑌂 𑌸𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌗𑍁𑌣𑌮𑍍।

8dcec7f554.b: Observed on Viśākhā nakshatra of Makaraḥ (sidereal solar) month (Prātaḥ/paraviddha).
8dcec7f554.d:
Between the 6th and 9th centuries, in South India, there existed 63 ardent devotees of Bhagavan Shiva, collectively known as the Nayanmars. These devout individuals, hailing from various walks of life including potters, fishermen, farmers, merchants, priests, hunters, and washermen, created devotional songs still sung by followers around the globe. Among these Nayanmars, Appar, Sambandar, and Sundarar, known for their Thevaram hymns, along with Manikkavasagar, are distinguished as the Samayacharyas or the ‘The Four’ (nālvar) revered teachers of the faith. They were instrumental in promoting the Shaiva Siddhanta philosophy and culture, effectively challenging the spread of Jainism and Buddhism. Their teachings centered around the concept that Shiva embodies love, and that embracing love for all beings and existence is essential in connecting with Shiva, the Supreme Being.

The 2nd of these Nayanmars was tirunīlakaṇṭha nāyanmār, a dedicated devotee of Bhagavan Shiva who lived in Chidambaram, and was a potter by profession. He revered Bhagavan Shiva's devotees and often gifted them with clay begging bowls he crafted, finding great joy in this service.

Tiru Neelakanta Nayanmar worshipped Bhagavan Shiva in his form as Neelakanta, drawing inspiration from the deity's act of consuming poison to protect the world. He believed fervently that those who sought refuge in Bhagavan Shiva would be absolved of their sins and attain His divine abode.

Despite his virtuous life, Neelakanta once succumbed to lust and visited a prostitute. His pious wife discerned this but chose to serve him as usual, resolving privately to abstain from sexual relations with him. When Neelakanta approached her passionately, she swore by Bhagavan Neelakanta and inadvertently used “us” instead of “me”. Taking her words to heart and their vow to Bhagavan Shiva, Neelakanta decided never to touch any woman again, a testament to his deep devotion.

The couple lived on, keeping their vow secret. As they aged, Bhagavan Shiva chose to unveil Neelakanta's spiritual greatness. Disguised as a Shiva Yogi, Bhagavan Shiva entrusted Neelakanta with a special bowl, claiming it could purify anything it touched. Later, when Bhagavan Shiva returned for the bowl, he miraculously made it disappear, leading Neelakanta to admit its loss. Accused of theft and unable to touch his wife due to their vow, the situation escalated to a court hearing.

At the court, Neelakanta revealed their secret of celibacy. As they held the ends of a stick and immersed themselves in a tank, a miracle occurred. They emerged youthful and radiant. Bhagavan Shiva and Mother Parvathy then appeared, declaring that due to their self-control and devotion, Neelakanta and his wife would live eternally youthful in the divine abode. This story showcases the power of devotion, celibacy, and the unassuming nature of true virtue.
8dcec7f554.r: - 63 Nayanmar Saints by Swami Sivananda, published by The Divine Life Society

𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌶𑍍𑌚𑍋𑌰𑍍𑌧𑍍𑌵𑌮𑌨𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌮𑌹𑌃 𑌸𑌙𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌮𑌣𑍇 𑌨𑌿𑌶𑌿।  
𑌦𑌿𑌵𑌾 𑌪𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌰𑌾 𑌰𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌰𑌿𑌤𑌿 𑌵𑍇𑌦𑌵𑌿𑌦𑍋 𑌵𑌿𑌦𑍁𑌃॥

8ddd45c7f1.d: Śaniḥ sets into combustion (astamayaH), heading prāk (east), on 2027-Mar-19 21:55. At this moment śaniḥ is at rēvatī-2 mīnaḥ (latitude 2°14′27.99″ S, moving r̥ju (direct)), magnitude +0.75, elongation 16°35′40.87″ E of the Sun. Combustion (mAudhyam) is generally considered to weaken a graha's ability to give full results in its significations; undertakings connected with śaniḥ are traditionally best avoided until it re-emerges.

8e133deb86.b: Observed on day 2 of Karkaṭaḥ (sidereal solar) month (Sūryōdayaḥ/puurvaviddha).
8e133deb86.d: One must not bathe in many (small) rivers during the rainy season. Especially for the first three days of Karkataka masa, these rivers are impure. However, this does not apply to the Mahanadis, owing to their greatness, including Ganga, Yamuna, Sarasvati, Godavari, Kaveri, Shona, Penna, and the Pancha Gangas (Kaveri, Tungabhadra, Krishnaveni, Gautami, Bhagirathi). Exceptions are made in the case of Upakarma, Utsarga, Grahanam, Preta snanam etc., and when new water can be mixed in these rivers, and when there is a lack of other water sources.
8e133deb86.s:
𑌅𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌃---  
𑌸𑌿𑌂𑌹𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌕𑌟𑌯𑍋𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌧𑍍𑌯𑍇 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌨𑌦𑍍𑌯𑍋 𑌰𑌜𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌲𑌾𑌃।  
𑌨 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌦𑍀𑌨𑌿 𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌣𑌿 𑌤𑌾𑌸𑍁 𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍀𑌤 𑌮𑌾𑌨𑌵𑌃॥  
𑌯𑍋𑌗𑌯𑌾𑌜𑍍𑌞𑌵𑌲𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌯𑌃---  
𑌰𑌜𑍋𑌦𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌟𑍇𑌽𑌮𑍍𑌭𑌸𑌿 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌜𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌨𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌷𑍁 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌜𑍈𑌃।  
𑌕𑌦𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌿𑌤𑌂 𑌰𑌜𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍇𑌷𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑌨𑍍𑌧𑍍𑌯𑍋𑌪𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌤𑌰𑍍𑌪𑌣𑌮𑍍  
𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌘𑍍𑌰𑌪𑌾𑌦𑌃---  
𑌸𑌿𑌂𑌹𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌕𑌟𑌯𑍋𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌧𑍍𑌯𑍇 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌨𑌦𑍍𑌯𑍋 𑌰𑌜𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌲𑌾𑌃।  
𑌤𑌾𑌸𑍁 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌨 𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍀𑌤 𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌜𑌯𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌸𑌮𑍁𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌗𑌾𑌃॥  
𑌕𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌨𑌃---  
𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌕𑌟𑌾𑌦𑍌 𑌰𑌜𑍋𑌦𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌾 𑌗𑍋𑌮𑌤𑍀 𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌰𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑌮𑍍।  
𑌚𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌭𑌾𑌗𑌾 𑌸𑌤𑍀 𑌸𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌧𑍁𑌃 𑌸𑌰𑌯𑍂𑌨𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌦𑌾 𑌤𑌥𑌾॥  
𑌅𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌮𑌾𑌹 𑌮𑌰𑍀𑌚𑌿𑌃---  
𑌆𑌦𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌦𑍁𑌹𑌿𑌤𑌾 𑌗𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌾 𑌪𑍍𑌲𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌜𑌾𑌤𑌾 𑌸𑌰𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌤𑍀।  
𑌰𑌜𑌸𑌾 𑌨𑌾𑌭𑌿𑌭𑍂𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍇 𑌯𑍇 𑌚𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌯𑍇 𑌨𑌦𑌸𑌂𑌜𑍍𑌞𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌃॥  
𑌮𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌕𑌣𑍍𑌡𑍇𑌯𑌃---  
𑌕𑌾𑌲𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍀 𑌗𑍌𑌤𑌮𑍀 𑌗𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌾 𑌵𑍇𑌣𑌿𑌕𑌾 𑌚 𑌸𑌰𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌤𑍀।  
𑌸𑌾𑌮𑌰𑍍𑌥𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑌾𑌭𑌿𑌜𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌚 𑌰𑌜𑍋 𑌨𑌾𑌭𑌿𑌭𑌵𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌮𑍂𑌃॥  
𑌜𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌨𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌭𑍂𑌤𑌾 𑌪𑍍𑌲𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌜𑌾𑌤𑌾 𑌸𑌰𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌤𑍀।  
𑌰𑌜𑌸𑌾 𑌨𑍈𑌵 𑌦𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌨𑌦𑌾𑌃 𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌾 𑌚 𑌵𑍇𑌣𑌿𑌕𑌾॥  
𑌵𑌾𑌮𑌨𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇---  
𑌸𑌰𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌤𑍀 𑌨𑌦𑍀 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌵𑍈𑌤𑌰𑌣𑍀 𑌨𑌦𑍀।  
𑌆𑌪𑌗𑌾 𑌚 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌗𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌾 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌦𑌾𑌕𑌿𑌨𑍀 𑌤𑌥𑌾॥  
𑌮𑌧𑍁𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌵𑌾𑌹𑌾𑌂𑌽𑌶𑍁𑌮𑌤𑍀 𑌕𑍌𑌶𑌿𑌕𑍀 𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌨𑌾𑌶𑌿𑌨𑍀।  
𑌦𑍃𑌷𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌤𑍀 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌵𑍈𑌤𑌰𑌣𑍀 𑌨𑌦𑍀॥  
𑌏𑌤𑌾𑌸𑌾𑌮𑍁𑌦𑌕𑌂 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌷𑌾𑌕𑌾𑌲𑍇 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌿𑌤𑌮𑍍।  
𑌰𑌜𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌲𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌮𑍇𑌤𑌾𑌸𑌾𑌂 𑌵𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌤𑍇 𑌨 𑌕𑌦𑌾𑌚𑌨॥  
𑌯𑌮𑌃---  
𑌗𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌾 𑌧𑌰𑍍𑌮𑍋𑌦𑍍𑌭𑌵𑌾 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌯𑌮𑍁𑌨𑌾 𑌚 𑌸𑌰𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌤𑍀।  
𑌅𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌰𑍍𑌗𑌤𑌰𑌜𑍋𑌯𑍋𑌗𑌾𑌃 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌹𑌃𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌪𑌿 𑌚𑌾𑌮𑌲𑌾𑌃॥  
𑌕𑌾𑌲𑌾𑌦𑌰𑍍𑌶𑌃---  
𑌸𑌿𑌂𑌹𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌕𑌟𑌯𑍋𑌰𑍍𑌨𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌃 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌏𑌵 𑌰𑌜𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌲𑌾𑌃।  
𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌂 𑌸𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌨𑌦𑍍𑌯𑍋 𑌗𑍋𑌦𑌾𑌂 𑌪𑍇𑌣𑍍𑌣𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑌰𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌤𑍀𑌮𑍍।  
𑌭𑌾𑌗𑍀𑌰𑌥𑍀𑌂 𑌚 𑌕𑌾𑌲𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍀 𑌨𑌦𑌾𑌨𑍍 𑌶𑍋𑌣𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌕𑌾𑌨𑍍 𑌵𑌿𑌨𑌾॥  
𑌕𑍇𑌚𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍁–--  
𑌯𑌾 𑌨𑌿𑌸𑍍𑌸𑍃𑌤𑌾 𑌨𑌦𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌾 𑌯𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌗𑌙𑍍𑌗𑍇𑌤𑌿 𑌕𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌃।  
𑌏𑌤𑌾𑌸𑌾𑌂 𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌕𑌟𑍇 𑌭𑌾𑌨𑍌 𑌰𑌜𑍋𑌦𑍋𑌷𑍋 𑌨 𑌵𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌤𑍇॥  
𑌕𑌾𑌵𑍇𑌰𑍀𑌤𑍁𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌭𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌾 𑌚 𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌵𑍇𑌣𑍀 𑌚 𑌗𑍌𑌤𑌮𑍀।  
𑌭𑌾𑌗𑍀𑌰𑌥𑍀 𑌚 𑌵𑌿𑌖𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌤𑌾 𑌪𑌞𑍍𑌚𑌗𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌕𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌃॥  
𑌕𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌨𑌃---  
𑌉𑌪𑌾𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌣𑌿 𑌚𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌗𑍇 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑍇 𑌤𑌥𑍈𑌵 𑌚।  
𑌚𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌸𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌗𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍇 𑌚𑍈𑌵 𑌰𑌜𑍋𑌦𑍋𑌷𑍋 𑌨 𑌵𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌤𑍇॥  
𑌮𑌹𑌦𑌮𑍍𑌬𑍁𑌸𑌮𑌂 𑌵𑌾𑌽𑌪𑌿 𑌯𑌦𑌿 𑌤𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌠𑍇𑌤𑍍 𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌤𑌨𑌮𑍍।  
𑌨𑌵𑌾𑌮𑍍𑌬𑍁 𑌮𑌿𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌤𑌂 𑌤𑍇𑌨 𑌨 𑌦𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌮𑌿𑌤𑌿 𑌸𑍂𑌰𑌯𑌃॥   
𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌘𑍍𑌰𑌪𑌾𑌦𑌃---  
𑌅𑌭𑌾𑌵𑍇 𑌕𑍂𑌪𑌵𑌾𑌪𑍀𑌨𑌾𑌮𑌨𑌪𑌾𑌯𑌿𑌪𑌯𑍋𑌭𑍃𑌤𑌾𑌮𑍍।  
𑌰𑌜𑍋𑌦𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌟𑍇𑌽𑌪𑌿 𑌪𑌯𑌸𑌿 𑌗𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌮𑌭𑍋𑌗𑍋 𑌨 𑌦𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌤𑌿॥

8e2763ab93.b: Observed on Śukla-Caturdaśī tithi of Mārgaśīrṣaḥ (lunar) month (Pūrvāhṇaḥ/paraviddha).
8e2763ab93.d: O great ascetic, today, on the fourteenth tithi of the bright half, in the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, The bathing and other rites performed here lead to the deliverance from the state of a Pishācha. Having bathed near Kapardīśvara on the fourteenth tithi of the bright half of Mārgaśīrṣa, And dying even elsewhere, one does not attain the state of a Pishacha. Those humans who perform this annual journey (yātrā), Will overcome the sins incurred by accepting gifts/fees at a sacred place (tīrtha-pratigrahāt pāpāt). Having bathed at the Pishācha-Mochana Tīrtha, and having duly worshipped Kapardīśa (https://maps.app.goo.gl/tnyPhvCrr4etPC7o7), And having performed the offering of food (annadāna), one becomes fearless both here (in this world) and hereafter. At the Pishācha-Mochana Tīrtha, one should raise/take a 'loṣṭadroṇa' [a measure/amount of water]—in the other world, they are not tormented even by a slight thirst. Thus, the Pishācha-Mochana Yātrā (pilgrimage) is described by the verses of the Skanda Sanatkumāra Saṃhitā in the work Kāśī-Tattva-Prakāśikā. Since the tithis of the forenoon (pūrvāhṇa) are auspicious for rites concerning the gods, the Chaturdashī (fourteenth tithi) that prevails in the forenoon is to be taken for the observance of this yātrā.
8e2763ab93.s:
𑌮𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌗𑌶𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌮𑍍---  
𑌅𑌦𑍍𑌯 𑌶𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌮𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌗𑍇 𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌿 𑌤𑌪𑍋𑌨𑌿𑌧𑍇।  
𑌅𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌸𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌕𑌂 𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌯 𑌪𑍈𑌶𑌾𑌚𑍍𑌯𑌪𑌰𑌿𑌮𑍋𑌚𑌨𑌮𑍍॥  
𑌮𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌗𑌶𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌕𑌪𑌰𑍍𑌦𑍀𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌰𑌸𑌨𑍍𑌨𑌿𑌧𑍌।  
𑌮𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌽𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌪𑌿 𑌮𑌰𑌣𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌨 𑌪𑍈𑌶𑌾𑌚𑍍𑌯𑌮𑌵𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌨𑍁𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍॥  
𑌇𑌮𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑌾𑌂𑌵𑌤𑍍𑌸𑌰𑍀 𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾 𑌯𑍇 𑌕𑌰𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌮𑌾𑌨𑌵𑌾𑌃।  
𑌤𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌿𑌗𑍍𑌰𑌹𑌾𑌤𑍍 𑌪𑌾𑌪𑌾𑌤𑍍 𑌤𑍇 𑌤𑌰𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌮𑌾𑌨𑌵𑌾𑌃॥  
𑌪𑍈𑌶𑌾𑌚𑌮𑍋𑌚𑌨𑍇 𑌸𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌕𑌪𑌰𑍍𑌦𑍀𑌶𑌂 𑌸𑌮𑌰𑍍𑌚𑍍𑌯 𑌚।  
𑌕𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌨𑌦𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌚 𑌇𑌹𑌾𑌮𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌚 𑌨𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌭𑌯𑌃॥  
𑌪𑌿𑌶𑌾𑌚𑌮𑍋𑌚𑌨𑍇 𑌤𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌥𑍇 𑌲𑍋𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌦𑍍𑌰𑍋𑌣𑌂 𑌸𑌮𑍁𑌦𑍍𑌧𑌰𑍇𑌤𑍍।  
𑌨 𑌪𑍀𑌡𑍍𑌯𑌤𑍇 𑌪𑌰𑍇 𑌲𑍋𑌕𑍇 𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌲𑍍𑌪𑌯𑌾𑌽𑌪𑌿 𑌪𑌿𑌪𑌾𑌸𑌯𑌾॥  
𑌇𑌤𑌿 𑌕𑌾𑌶𑍀𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌕𑌾𑌶𑌿𑌕𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑍍𑌕𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌦𑌸𑌨𑌤𑍍𑌕𑍁𑌮𑌾𑌰𑌸𑌂𑌹𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌵𑌚𑌨𑍈𑌃 𑌪𑌿𑌶𑌾𑌚𑌮𑍋𑌚𑌨𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍋𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌾। 𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌰  
``𑌪𑍌𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌣𑌿𑌕𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌤𑌿𑌥𑌯𑍋 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌯𑍇 𑌶𑍁𑌭𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌦𑌾𑌃॥'' 𑌇𑌤𑌿𑌵𑌚𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌪𑍌𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌣𑌿𑌕𑍀 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌦𑌶𑍀 𑌗𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌯𑌾।

8f0b99f616.s:
𑌮𑌦𑌨𑌰𑌤𑍍𑌨𑍇 𑌭𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌯𑍇---  
𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣 𑌉𑌵𑌾𑌚---  
𑌶𑍇𑌤𑍇 𑌜𑌗𑌤𑍍𑌪𑌤𑌿𑌃 𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌃 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌯𑌾 𑌸𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌧𑌂 𑌯𑌦𑌾 𑌨𑍃𑌪।  
𑌅𑌶𑍂𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌶𑌯𑌨𑌾 𑌨𑌾𑌮 𑌤𑌦𑌾 𑌗𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌤𑍁 𑌸𑌾 𑌤𑌿𑌥𑌿𑌃॥  
𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌤𑍀𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌵𑌣𑍇 𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌿 𑌭𑌾𑌰𑌤।  
(𑌅𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌿𑌨𑍍 𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑍇 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌵𑌣𑌃 𑌶𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍋 𑌗𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌯𑌃।)  
𑌵𑌾𑌮𑌨𑌪𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑍇---  
𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌤𑌿𑌥𑌿𑌷𑍁 𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌮𑍇𑌣 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌕𑍃𑌷𑍍𑌣-𑌕𑌾𑌮-𑌯𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍋-𑌮𑌾𑌪𑌤𑌿-𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌹𑍍𑌮-𑌵𑌿𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌣𑌾𑌂 𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌪𑌮𑌭𑌿𑌧𑌾𑌯---  
𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌤𑌿𑌥𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌪𑌿𑌤𑌿 𑌵𑌿𑌶𑍍𑌵𑌕𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌾 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌜𑌾𑌪𑌤𑌿𑌃।  
𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌤𑍀𑌯𑌾 𑌸𑌾 𑌶𑍁𑌭𑌾 𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌸𑍁𑌪𑍁𑌣𑍍𑌯𑌶𑌯𑌨𑍋𑌚𑌿𑌤𑌾॥  
𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌤𑌿𑌥𑌾𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌚𑍍𑌯 𑌹𑌰𑌿𑌂 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌵𑌤𑍍𑌸𑌾𑌙𑍍𑌕𑌂 𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌭𑌜𑌮𑍍।  
𑌪𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌙𑍍𑌕𑌸𑍍𑌥𑌂 𑌸𑌮𑌂 𑌲𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌗𑌨𑍍𑌧𑌪𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌪𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌭𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌮𑍁𑌨𑍇॥  
𑌤𑌤𑍋 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌾𑌯 𑌶𑌯𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌫𑌲𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌿𑌪𑍇𑌤𑍍𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌮𑌾𑌤𑍍।  
𑌇𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌾 𑌆𑌷𑌾𑌢𑍍𑌯𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌵𑌹𑌿𑌤𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌤𑍀𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌮𑍇𑌵𑌾𑌭𑌿𑌧𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍍।  
𑌇𑌮𑌮𑍁𑌚𑍍𑌚𑌾𑌰𑌯𑍇𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌣𑌮𑍍𑌯 𑌚 𑌜𑌗𑌤𑍍𑌪𑌤𑌿𑌮𑍍---  
𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌵𑌤𑍍𑌸𑌧𑌾𑌰𑌿 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌕𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌵𑌾𑌸 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌪𑌤𑍇𑌽𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌯।  
𑌗𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌥𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌮𑌾 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌣𑌾𑌶𑌂 𑌮𑍇 𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍁 𑌧𑌰𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌕𑌾𑌮𑌦𑌮𑍍॥  
𑌶𑍁𑌚𑌯𑍋 𑌮𑌾 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌣𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌮𑌾 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌣𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌨𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌜𑌰𑌾𑌃।  
𑌯𑌾𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌗𑌾 𑌮𑌾 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌣𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌮𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍋 𑌦𑌮𑍍𑌪𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌭𑍇𑌦𑌤𑌃॥  
(𑌶𑍁𑌚𑌯𑍋𑌽𑌗𑍍𑌨𑌯𑌃। 𑌨𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌜𑌰𑌾 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌾𑌃। 𑌯𑌾𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌗𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑌿𑌤𑌰𑌃।)  
𑌲𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌵𑌿𑌯𑍁𑌜𑍍𑌯𑌤𑍇 𑌦𑍇𑌵 𑌨 𑌕𑌦𑌾𑌚𑌿𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌥𑌾 𑌭𑌵𑌾𑌨𑍍।  
𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌕𑌲𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌬𑌨𑍍𑌧𑍋 𑌦𑍇𑌵 𑌮𑌾 𑌮𑍇 𑌵𑌿𑌯𑍁𑌜𑍍𑌯𑌤𑌾𑌮𑍍॥  
𑌲𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌨 𑌶𑍂𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌵𑌰𑌦 𑌯𑌥𑌾 𑌤𑍇 𑌶𑌯𑌨𑌂 𑌸𑌦𑌾।  
𑌶𑌯𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌮𑌮𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌯𑌶𑍂𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌤𑌥𑌾𑌽𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌮𑌧𑍁𑌸𑍂𑌦𑌨।  
𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌰𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌯𑍇 𑌤𑍁---  
𑌪𑌤𑍍𑌨𑍀 𑌭𑌰𑍍𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌯𑍋𑌗𑌂 𑌚 𑌭𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌾 𑌭𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌸𑌮𑍁𑌦𑍍𑌭𑌵𑌮𑍍।  
𑌨𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌨𑍁𑌵𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌯𑌥𑌾 𑌦𑍁𑌃𑌖𑌂 𑌦𑌮𑍍𑌪𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍁॥  
𑌯𑌥𑌾 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌿𑌯𑌾 𑌯𑍁𑌤𑍋 𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌲𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌮𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌦𑍇𑌵 𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌯𑌾 𑌯𑌥𑌾।  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌸𑌾𑌦𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌵 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑍇𑌶 𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌿𑌰𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌤𑌥𑌾𑌽𑌽𑌵𑌯𑍋𑌃॥  
𑌮𑌾 𑌸𑍍𑌮 𑌪𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌣𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌮𑌾 𑌧𑌨𑌂 𑌮𑌾 𑌕𑍁𑌲𑌕𑍍𑌰𑌮𑌃।  
𑌅𑌗𑍍𑌨𑌯𑍋 𑌮𑌾 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌣𑌶𑍍𑌯𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌗𑍃𑌹𑌭𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌮𑌾𑌽𑌽𑌵𑌯𑍋𑌃॥ 𑌇𑌤𑍍𑌯𑍇𑌤𑍇 𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌃।  
𑌏𑌵𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌸𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯 𑌪𑍂𑌜𑌾𑌂 𑌚 𑌕𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌲𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌹𑌰𑍇𑌃।  
𑌚𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌘𑍍𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌦𑍇𑌯𑍋 𑌦𑌧𑍍𑌯𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌤𑌫𑌲𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌭𑌿𑌃।  
𑌅𑌰𑍍𑌘𑍍𑌯𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌃---  
𑌗𑌗𑌨𑌾𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌣𑌸𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍀𑌪 𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍀𑌰𑌾𑌬𑍍𑌧𑌿𑌮𑌥𑌨𑍋𑌦𑍍𑌭𑌵।  
𑌭𑌾𑌭𑌾𑌸𑌿𑌤𑌦𑌿𑌗𑌾𑌭𑍋𑌗 𑌰𑌮𑌾𑌨𑍁𑌜 𑌨𑌮𑍋𑌽𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌤𑍇॥ 𑌇𑌤𑌿।  
𑌨𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌂 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌣𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌯𑌤𑌨𑍇 𑌹𑌰𑌿𑌂 𑌭𑍁𑌞𑍍𑌜𑍀𑌤 𑌵𑌾𑌗𑍍𑌯𑌤𑌃।  
𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌣𑌾𑌯 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌤𑍀𑌯𑍇𑌽𑌹𑍍𑌨𑌿 𑌶𑌯𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌦𑍇𑌯𑌾𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌦𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌿𑌣𑌾𑌃॥  
𑌯𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌮𑌹𑌾𑌬𑌾𑌹𑍋 𑌕𑌾𑌲𑍇 𑌸𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌫𑌲𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌚।  
𑌮𑌧𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑌿 𑌨 𑌤𑍀𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌣𑌿 𑌨 𑌚𑌾𑌪𑌿 𑌕𑌟𑍁𑌕𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌚॥  
𑌦𑌾𑌤𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌨𑍃𑌪𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍇𑌷𑍍𑌠 𑌸𑍍𑌵𑌶𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌶𑌯𑌨𑍇𑌽𑌨𑌘।  
𑌮𑌧𑍁𑌰𑌾𑌣𑌿 𑌚 𑌦𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾 𑌤𑍁 𑌮𑌨𑍋𑌵𑌲𑍍𑌲𑌭𑌤𑌾𑌂 𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌜𑍇𑌤𑍍।  
𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌕𑌟𑍁𑌕𑌤𑍀𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌣𑌿 𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌲𑌿𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌚 𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌜𑌯𑍇𑌤𑍍॥  
𑌖𑌰𑍍𑌜𑍂𑌰𑌮𑌾𑌤𑍁𑌲𑌿𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌸𑍍𑌥𑌿𑌤𑍇𑌨 𑌶𑌿𑌰𑌸𑌾 𑌸𑌹।  
(𑌸𑍍𑌥𑌿𑌤𑍇𑌨 𑌶𑌿𑌰𑌸𑌾 𑌦𑍃𑌢𑌨𑌾𑌰𑍀𑌕𑍇𑌲𑌫𑌲𑍇𑌨𑍇𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌰𑍍𑌥𑌃।)  
𑌏𑌤𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌯𑍇𑌵 𑌤𑍁 𑌵𑌿𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌗𑌾𑌙𑍍𑌗𑍇𑌯 𑌸𑌹𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌚॥  
𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌤𑍀𑌯𑍇𑌽𑌹𑍍𑌨𑌿 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌦𑍇𑌯𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌶𑌕𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌚 𑌭𑌾𑌰𑌤।  
𑌵𑌾𑌸𑍋𑌦𑌾𑌨𑌂 𑌤𑌥𑌾 𑌧𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌫𑌲𑌦𑌾𑌨𑌸𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌤𑌮𑍍॥  
𑌏𑌵𑌂 𑌕𑌰𑍋𑌤𑌿 𑌯𑌃 𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌙𑍍𑌨𑌰𑍋 𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌯𑌮𑍍।  
𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌜𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌯𑌂 𑌵𑍀𑌰 𑌗𑍃𑌹𑌭𑌙𑍍𑌗𑍋 𑌨 𑌜𑌾𑌯𑌤𑍇॥ 𑌇𑌤𑌿।  
𑌪𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌮𑍇---  
𑌗𑍀𑌤𑌵𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌨𑌿𑌰𑍍𑌘𑍋𑌷𑌂 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌕𑌾𑌰𑌯𑍇𑌤𑍍।  
𑌘𑌣𑍍𑌟𑌾 𑌵𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌮𑌶𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌸𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌵𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌮𑌯𑍀 𑌯𑌤𑌃॥  
𑌏𑌵𑌂 𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌪𑍂𑌜𑍍𑌯 𑌗𑍋𑌵𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌦𑌮𑌶𑍍𑌨𑍀𑌯𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍈𑌲𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌜𑌿𑌤𑌮𑍍।  
𑌨𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌮𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌾𑌰𑌲𑌵𑌣𑌂 𑌯𑌾𑌵𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌟𑌯𑌮𑍍॥  
𑌤𑌤𑌃 𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌭𑌾𑌤𑍇 𑌸𑌞𑍍𑌜𑌾𑌤𑍇 𑌲𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌮𑍀𑌪𑌤𑌿𑌸𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌮𑍍।  
𑌦𑍀𑌪𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌨𑌭𑍋𑌜𑌨𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌂 𑌶𑌯𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌦𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌚𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌣𑌃॥  
𑌪𑌾𑌦𑍁𑌕𑍋𑌪𑌾𑌨𑌹𑌚𑍍𑌛𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌚𑌾𑌮𑌰𑌾𑌸𑌨𑌸𑌂𑌯𑍁𑌤𑌾𑌮𑍍।  
𑌅𑌭𑍀𑌷𑍍𑌟𑍋𑌪𑌸𑍍𑌕𑌰𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌾𑌂 𑌶𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑌪𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌪𑌾𑌮𑍍𑌬𑌰𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌵𑍃𑌤𑌾𑌮𑍍॥  
𑌸𑍋𑌪𑌧𑌾𑌨𑌕𑌵𑌿𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌮𑌾𑌂 𑌫𑌲𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌵𑌿𑌧𑍈𑌰𑍍𑌯𑍁𑌤𑌾𑌮𑍍।  
𑌤𑌥𑌾𑌽𑌽𑌭𑌰𑌣𑌧𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌯𑍈𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌯𑌥𑌾𑌶𑌕𑍍𑌤𑌿-𑌸𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌮𑍍॥  
𑌅𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌙𑍍𑌗𑌾 𑌗𑍌𑌶𑍍𑌚 𑌵𑌿𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌯 𑌵𑍈𑌷𑍍𑌣𑌵𑌾𑌯 𑌕𑍁𑌟𑍁𑌮𑍍𑌬𑌿𑌨𑍇।  
𑌦𑌾𑌤𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌵𑍇𑌦𑌵𑌿𑌦𑍁𑌷𑍇 𑌨 𑌬𑌕𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌿𑌨𑍇 𑌕𑍍𑌵𑌚𑌿𑌤𑍍॥  
𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍋𑌪𑌵𑍇𑌶𑍍𑌯 𑌦𑌮𑍍𑌪𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌮𑌲𑌙𑍍𑌕𑍃𑌤𑍍𑌯 𑌵𑌿𑌧𑌾𑌨𑌤𑌃।  
𑌪𑌤𑍍𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌭𑍋𑌜𑌨𑌂 𑌦𑌦𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑍍𑌭𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌭𑍋𑌜𑍍𑌯𑌸𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌤𑌮𑍍॥  
𑌬𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌮𑌣𑌸𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌪𑌿 𑌸𑍌𑌵𑌰𑍍𑌣𑍀𑌮𑍁𑌪𑌸𑍍𑌕𑌰𑌸𑌮𑌨𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌤𑌾𑌮𑍍।  
𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌿𑌮𑌾𑌂 𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌦𑍇𑌵𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌸𑍋𑌦𑌕𑍁𑌮𑍍𑌭𑌾𑌂 𑌨𑌿𑌵𑍇𑌦𑌯𑍇𑌤𑍍॥  
𑌏𑌵𑌂 𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌤𑍁 𑌪𑍁𑌮𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌦𑌶𑍂𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌶𑌯𑌨𑌂 𑌹𑌰𑍇𑌃।  
𑌨 𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌯 𑌵𑌿𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌵𑌿𑌰𑌹𑌃 𑌕𑌦𑌾𑌚𑌿𑌦𑌪𑌿 𑌜𑌾𑌯𑌤𑍇।  
𑌨𑌾𑌰𑍀 𑌵𑌾 𑌵𑌿𑌧𑌵𑌾 𑌰𑌾𑌜𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌵𑌚𑍍𑌚𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌕𑌤𑌾𑌰𑌕𑌮𑍍। 𑌇𑌤𑌿।  
𑌮𑌾𑌤𑍍𑌸𑍍𑌯𑍇---  
𑌨 𑌵𑌿𑌰𑍂𑌪𑌂 𑌨 𑌶𑍋𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌤𑌂 𑌦𑌮𑍍𑌪𑌤𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌜𑌾𑌯𑌤𑍇 𑌕𑍍𑌵𑌚𑌿𑌤𑍍।  
𑌨 𑌪𑍁𑌤𑍍𑌰𑌪𑌶𑍁𑌰𑌤𑍍𑌨𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌕𑍍𑌷𑌯𑌂 𑌯𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌤𑌿 𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌜𑍋𑌤𑍍𑌤𑌮॥  
𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌕𑌲𑍍𑌪𑌸𑌹𑌸𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌣𑌿 𑌸𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌕𑌲𑍍𑌪𑌶𑌤𑌾𑌨𑌿 𑌚।  
𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌨𑍍𑌨𑌶𑍂𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌶𑌯𑌨𑌂 𑌸𑍂𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌲𑍋𑌕𑍇 𑌮𑌹𑍀𑌯𑌤𑍇॥ 𑌇𑌤𑌿।  
𑌅𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌿𑌨𑍍 𑌚𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑍋𑌦𑌯𑍇 𑌪𑍂𑌜𑌾𑌵𑌿𑌧𑌾𑌨𑌾𑌚𑍍𑌚𑌨𑍍𑌦𑍍𑌰𑍋𑌦𑌯𑌵𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌪𑌿𑌨𑍍𑌯𑍇𑌵 𑌤𑌿𑌥𑌿 𑌗𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌹𑍍𑌯𑌾। 𑌦𑌿𑌨𑌦𑍍𑌵𑌯𑍇𑌽𑌪𑌿 𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌸𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌾𑌸𑌤𑍍𑌤𑍍𑌵𑌯𑍋𑌃 𑌪𑌰𑍈𑌵।  
𑌚𑌤𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌵𑌸𑌿𑌤𑌪𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍇𑌷𑍁 𑌮𑌾𑌸𑍇𑌷𑍁 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌵𑌣𑌾𑌦𑌿𑌷𑍁।  
𑌅𑌶𑍂𑌨𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌖𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌵𑍍𑌰𑌤𑌂 𑌕𑍁𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌜𑍍𑌜𑌯𑌯𑌾 𑌤𑍁 𑌫𑌲𑌾𑌧𑌿𑌕𑌮𑍍। 𑌇𑌤𑌿 𑌵𑌚𑌨𑌾𑌤𑍍।

8f721c4eb2.b: Observed on Śukla-Pañcamī tithi of Caitraḥ (lunar) month (Sūryōdayaḥ/puurvaviddha).
8f721c4eb2.s:
𑌶𑍁𑌕𑍍𑌲𑌾𑌯𑌾𑌮𑌥 𑌪𑌞𑍍𑌚𑌮𑍍𑌯𑌾𑌂 𑌚𑍈𑌤𑍍𑌰𑍇 𑌮𑌾𑌸𑌿 𑌶𑍁𑌭𑌾𑌨𑌨𑌾।  
𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌲𑍋𑌕𑌾𑌨𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌨𑍁𑌷𑍍𑌯𑌂 𑌸𑌮𑍍𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌾𑌪𑍍𑌤𑌾 𑌕𑍇𑌶𑌵𑌾𑌜𑍍𑌞𑌯𑌾॥  
𑌤𑌸𑍍𑌮𑌾𑌤𑍍 𑌤𑌾𑌂 𑌪𑍂𑌜𑌯𑍇𑌤𑍍 𑌤𑌤𑍍𑌰 𑌯𑌸𑍍𑌤𑌂 𑌲𑌕𑍍𑌷𑍍𑌮𑍀𑌰𑍍𑌨 𑌮𑍁𑌞𑍍𑌚𑌤𑌿।  
𑌏𑌷𑌾 𑌶𑍍𑌰𑍀𑌪𑌞𑍍𑌚𑌮𑍀 𑌕𑌾𑌰𑍍𑌯𑌾 𑌵𑌿𑌷𑍍𑌣𑍁𑌲𑍋𑌕𑌗𑌤𑌿𑌪𑍍𑌰𑌦𑌾॥

8f842a6401.b: Observed on day 1 of Kanyā (sidereal solar) month (Sūryōdayaḥ/puurvaviddha).
